meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 7, 2019 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Convening on October 7, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council honored the late Omega Curtis Parker, welcomed Durham Neighborhood College participants, and issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Indigenous Peoples' Day, and World Food Day before unanimously approving the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18). On Item 14 (505 West Chapel Hill Street disposition), Charlie Reece disclosed that his family's company, Rho Inc., and competing developer Everage Group both used Joyce Fitzpatrick Communications—which City Attorney Kim Rehberg ruled was not a disqualifying financial interest—and Council voted 7-0 to reopen a staff-vetted amendment window for both Fallon and Everage until October 18 ahead of a November 4 vote. Council then passed pulled Item 15 (Center for Documentary Studies Full Frame contract) and Item 17 (HUD Fair Housing Assistance funding) 7-0, before approving Item 18 (Made in Durham youth program contract modification) by a 5-2 split vote, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Charlie Reece and DeDreana Freeman voting No to support a resident's request for a delay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Omega Curtis Parker Tribute, Proclamations, and Election Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting with Spanish interpretation instructions from Javiera Caballero and a moment of silent meditation honoring former school board member and DPS librarian Omega Curtis Parker. Council welcomed the 2019 Durham Neighborhood College cohort and issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month (Caballero), Indigenous Peoples' Day on October 14 (DeDreana Freeman), and World Food Day / Neighbors Feeding Neighbors Day on October 16 (Mark-Anthony Middleton). Council Members Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Vernetta Alston, and Mark-Anthony Middleton offered announcements regarding the October 8 at-large primary election, grassroots anti-gun violence work by BOSS and Bull City Ceasefire, and election-day fare-free transit.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items. Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, performance audits, HUD CDBG excess program income return, DCLT loan modifications for West Park and Morehead Glenn Apartments, transit demand-response merger, election-day fare-free bus ordinance, NC State TRM agreement, Old Chapel Hill Road waterline contract, August 2019 bid report, hybrid police vehicles, American Dance Festival contract, and Summit Design land surveying amendment. Items 15, 17, and 18 were pulled, and Council approved the remaining Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Updated Disposition Process for 505 West Chapel Hill Street (Former Police Headquarters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece read an ethics disclosure stating that Fitzpatrick Communications worked independently for both his family's company (Rho Inc.) and developer Everage Group, and confirmed City Attorney Kim Rehberg determined no disqualifying financial interest existed so he was legally required to participate. Mayor Steve Schewel proposed giving both competing development teams (Fallon Group and Everage Group) until October 18, 2019 at close of business to submit any substantive amendments directly to staff, followed by staff vetting and a Council vote on November 4, 2019. DeDreana Freeman questioned whether accepting post-deadline submissions violated the closed June 28 RFP process, while Mark-Anthony Middleton emphasized Council had not yet voted on a developer and needed complete vetted information; Council approved the extension 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 15 to ask General Services staff Stacey Poston about the five new evaluation criteria used with the Cultural Advisory Board and Discover Durham's Festivals and Events Committee. Freeman urged adding racial equity criteria in future funding cycles to address underfunding of Afrocentric cultural events, and Poston agreed to incorporate that feedback next year. Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 17 had been pulled by public speakers Tyrone Savage and Dennis Garrett. Mayor Schewel called both speakers' names, and neither was present in the chamber. Council moved and seconded approval of the HUD Fair Housing Assistance agreement, passing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece pulled Item 18 after a resident emailed requesting a delay to review Made in Durham performance materials. Office of Economic and Workforce Development staffer Majora Graham-Scott and City Manager Tom Bonfield warned that a delay would create financial hardship for Made in Durham since the contract period began July 1 and work-based collaborative programming toward 600 Durham YouthWorks internships had already launched. DeDreana Freeman echoed community concerns about whether Made in Durham was reaching intended youth and supported delaying the vote, while Reece read from the resident's email criticizing deviations in service model and internship yield; Council approved the contract modification 5-2, with Reece changing his vote from not voting to No to honor the resident's delay request.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-13, 16, and 19, excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
votes.discussion_detail: With Items 15, 17, and 18 pulled from the consent slate, Council approved the remaining Consent Agenda items—including appointments, performance audits, DCLT loan modifications, transit demand-response merger, general election fare-free transit, waterline and surveying contracts, and police hybrid vehicles—by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 14 — Extend 505 West Chapel Hill Street Proposal Submission Window to October 18 and Defer Vote to November 4, 2019
votes.discussion_detail: Following Charlie Reece's ethics disclosure and discussion of late developer communications outside the closed June 28 RFP process, Council voted 7-0 to give both Fallon and Everage until close of business on October 18, 2019 to submit any amendments to staff, direct staff to vet and brief Council, and schedule a vote for November 4, 2019.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
votes.discussion_detail: After DeDreana Freeman questioned General Services staff Stacey Poston about adding racial equity criteria for Afrocentric cultural events in future festival funding cycles, Council unanimously approved the contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Approve U.S. HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Neither registered speaker (Tyrone Savage or Dennis Garrett) was present when Item 17 was called; Council moved, seconded, and approved the HUD Fair Housing Assistance agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18 — Authorize City Manager to Execute Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
votes.notes: Charlie Reece initially registered as not voting and asked the clerk to record his vote as No, bringing the final tally to 5-2.
votes.discussion_detail: After debate over a resident's last-minute request to delay consideration and concerns raised by DeDreana Freeman regarding target youth reach, Council approved the contract modification 5-2. The vote initially registered 5-1 with one member not voting before Charlie Reece requested changing his non-vote to No to give voice to the resident requesting a delay while noting he supported the contract.

disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Delay of Made in Durham Youth Program Contract Modification (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to immediately authorize the Made in Durham contract modification or delay action to allow further review of a resident's critique of the organization's service model and internship outcomes.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the contract modification immediately to avoid financial hardship on an ongoing workforce partnership.
side_a_arguments: The contract period began July 1 and Made in Durham's work-based collaborative supporting 600 Durham YouthWorks internships had already launched.
Staff and the City Manager warned delaying approval would create financial hardship for the organization and noted the item had already gone through the regular work session review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay consideration of the contract modification to examine community concerns about outcomes and target youth reach.
side_b_arguments: A resident asked for additional time to review materials regarding Made in Durham's deviation from its original service model and limited internship yield relative to applicants.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 7, 2019 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: In the closed-captioned broadcast of the October 7, 2019 Durham City Council meeting with all seven members present, Council remembered former school board member Omega Curtis Parker, recognized Durham Neighborhood College participants, and presented proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Indigenous Peoples' Day, and World Food Day before adopting the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18). On Item 14 (505 West Chapel Hill Street disposition), Charlie Reece placed on the record City Attorney Kim Rehberg's ruling that shared use of Fitzpatrick Communications by his family's firm (Rho Inc.) and developer Everage Group created no disqualifying conflict, and Council voted 7-0 to reopen a staff-vetted amendment window through October 18 ahead of a November 4 vote. Council approved pulled Item 15 (Center for Documentary Studies contract) and Item 17 (HUD Fair Housing Assistance funding) 7-0, then passed Item 18 (Made in Durham youth program contract modification) by a 5-2 vote with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Charlie Reece and DeDreana Freeman voting No.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Omega Curtis Parker Tribute, Proclamations, and Election Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, had Javiera Caballero announce Spanish interpretation availability, and led a moment of silent meditation honoring former school board member Omega Curtis Parker. Council welcomed the 2019 Durham Neighborhood College class and presented proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Indigenous Peoples' Day (October 14), and World Food Day / Neighbors Feeding Neighbors Day (October 16). Members then shared announcements about the October 8 at-large city primary, grassroots violence-prevention work, and election-day fare-free bus service.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk confirmed they had no priority items. Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, June 2019 audits, HUD CDBG excess program income return, DCLT loan modifications, transit demand-response merger, election-day fare-free transit, NC State TRM agreement, Old Chapel Hill Road waterline contract, August 2019 bid report, hybrid police vehicles, American Dance Festival contract, and land surveying amendment. Excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18, Council approved the Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Updated Disposition Process for 505 West Chapel Hill Street (Former Police Headquarters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece disclosed that his family business, Rho Inc., and competing developer Everage Group had both retained Joyce Fitzpatrick Communications, and read City Attorney Kim Rehberg's determination that no disqualifying financial interest existed, making his vote mandatory. Mayor Schewel proposed giving both Fallon and Everage until close of business on October 18, 2019 to submit any substantive amendments to staff for vetting ahead of a November 4 vote. DeDreana Freeman questioned reopening a closed RFP process while Mark-Anthony Middleton affirmed Council's authority to gather complete vetted information before entering negotiations; Council passed the extension 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 15 to ask General Services staff Stacey Poston about the new five-element evaluation framework developed with Discover Durham and the Cultural Advisory Board. Freeman urged incorporating racial equity criteria so Afrocentric cultural events receive fair support, and Poston agreed to include that input in next year's review. Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 17 was pulled for registered public speakers Tyrone Savage and Dennis Garrett, neither of whom was present in the chamber when called. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece pulled Item 18 after receiving an email two hours before the meeting from a resident seeking a delay to review Made in Durham performance records. Majora Graham-Scott and City Manager Tom Bonfield explained the contract began July 1 and delaying it would cause financial hardship for ongoing Durham YouthWorks collaboration. DeDreana Freeman supported a delay to examine equity and target-youth concerns, and Reece read the resident's critique of service-model deviations; Council approved the contract modification 5-2 after Reece changed his initial non-vote to No.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-13, 16, and 19, excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
votes.discussion_detail: After pulling Items 15, 17, and 18, Council unanimously approved the remaining Consent Agenda items by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 14 — Extend 505 West Chapel Hill Street Proposal Submission Window to October 18 and Defer Vote to November 4, 2019
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 7-0 to reopen a staff-channeled amendment window through October 18, 2019 for both Fallon Group and Everage Group, direct staff to vet submissions, and take up the disposition vote on November 4, 2019.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
votes.discussion_detail: Following DeDreana Freeman's inquiry about adding racial equity criteria for cultural festival grants, Council approved the Center for Documentary Studies contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Approve U.S. HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: With neither registered speaker present, Council unanimously approved the HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program funding agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18 — Authorize City Manager to Execute Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
votes.notes: Charlie Reece initially registered as not voting and asked the clerk to record his vote as No, bringing the final tally to 5-2.
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the Made in Durham contract modification 5-2 after initially recording 5-1 with one not voting, which Charlie Reece corrected to No to give voice to a resident's request for a delay while affirming he supported the contract.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Oct 7, 2019 (with closed captions)
disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Delay of Made in Durham Youth Program Contract Modification (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 over whether to approve the Made in Durham youth program contract modification immediately or delay the vote to examine a resident's concerns about performance and target-youth reach.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the contract modification immediately to prevent financial disruption to ongoing youth workforce programming.
side_a_arguments: The contract period started July 1 and the work-based collaborative supporting Durham YouthWorks' 600-internship goal was already underway.
Delaying execution would create financial hardship for Made in Durham after the item had already passed work session review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay the vote to give community members and Council more time to assess service-model deviations and youth reach.
side_b_arguments: A resident requested more time to review performance materials alleging deviations from the original service model and insufficient internship yield.
DeDreana Freeman raised concerns over whether intended Black-owned businesses and target youth populations were actually being reached.
disagreements.resolution: Contract modification passed 5-2; Charlie Reece stated afterward he supported the contract and voted No solely to reflect the resident's request for a delay.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 16, 2019 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: Convening on September 16, 2019 with four members present—Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero—Council voted 4-0 to grant excused absences to ill Council Members Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman (alongside Mark-Anthony Middleton's previously excused absence). Following six ceremonial recognitions including a Sister City agreement with Sibiu, Romania and proclamations on hunger, diaper need, and preparedness, Council voted 4-0 in open session to approve performance-review salaries for City Clerk Diana Schreiber ($97,335) and City Manager Tom Bonfield ($255,191). Council then unanimously adopted the Consent Agenda 4-0 (excluding pulled Items 19 and 20) and approved pulled Item 19 (MS4 stormwater inspections) and Item 20 (Alleyway 13 stormwater repairs) 4-0 after discussion of contractor demographics and Duke campus runoff. In six consecutive public hearings on land-use and annexation applications—Items 23 (New Haven Townhouses), 24 (Magnolia Creek Phase 4), 25 (All Saints United Methodist Church), 26 (5510 Barbee Chapel Road / International Montessori School), 27 (Huntington Valley), and 28 (Hopewell Academy)—the four present members passed every required annexation, FLUM, consistency, and rezoning motion unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absences for Council Members Alston and Freeman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the clerk recorded four members present: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero. Schewel noted Mark-Anthony Middleton had a prior excused absence and both Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman were out ill, and Council voted 4-0 to grant Alston and Freeman excused absences.

agenda_items.title: Sibiu Sister City Agreement, Hunger/Preparedness Proclamations, Neighbor Spotlight, and Early Voting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council celebrated a Sister City partnership with Sibiu, Romania (including remarks from Sibiu's mayor), proclaimed Senior Hunger Awareness Week, Hunger Free Durham Month (highlighting free DPS breakfast and 117 summer meal sites), Diaper Need Awareness Week, and National Preparedness Month, heard historian Eddie Davis on Sam Reed, and presented the Neighbor Spotlight to Marcella Thompson of the Mustard Seed Project. Charlie Reece announced that two weeks of early voting for the October 8 primary would open Wednesday, September 18.

agenda_items.title: Approval of City Clerk and City Manager Salaries Following Annual Performance Reviews
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel reported that Council conducted annual performance reviews for City Clerk Diana Schreiber and City Manager Tom Bonfield in closed session (having just hired the City Attorney) and found both performed excellently. As required by law, Council voted in open session 4-0 to approve salaries with raises of $97,335 for the City Clerk and $255,191 for the City Manager.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 19 and 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager (represented by Deputy City Manager Wanda Page), City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items. On a point of order by Charlie Reece, Mayor Schewel agreed to take pulled Item 19 immediately rather than holding it until the end of the meeting, while resident Mr. Andrews pulled Item 20. Remaining consent items—including board appointments, Community Safety Task Force discussion, Affordable Housing Bond Advisory Committee report, Urban Ministries rapid rehousing amendment, electric bus procurement, Cornwallis Road sidewalks, garage security guards, cultural art changes, drainage/stormwater contracts, and scrap tire recycling—passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Inspections Contracts (SD-2019-06 & SD-2019-07)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece pulled Item 19 to explain that while work session discussion raised concerns over the demographics of one selected contractor, staff confirmed no subcontracting opportunities existed for specialized sewer inspections and no certified MWBE firms in the city database perform this specific service. Reece moved approval so critical stormwater inspection work could proceed, and Council passed it 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Infrastructure Repairs SD-2019-02 Amendment #2 (Alleyway 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Mr. Andrews supported fixing sinkholes along Alleyway 13 blocking schoolchildren, but warned that 35 acres of impervious runoff from Duke's campus overwhelmed the 100-year-old 24-inch pipe and caused repeated flooding on his property near Buchanan Boulevard. Public Works staffer Dana Hornkohl acknowledged legacy infrastructure limits and committed to following up with Andrews on regional stormwater planning; Council approved the contract amendment 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Item: New Haven Townhouses (2600 Ellis Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's request to amend the Future Land Use Map from Industrial/Open Space to Low-Medium Density Residential and rezone 9.116 acres at 2600 Ellis Road from RS-20 to PDR 6.239 for up to 55 townhouses (recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission). Edens proffered $8,250 ($150/unit) to Durham's Affordable Housing Fund prior to first final plan. Council approved the FLUM amendment, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Zoning Map Change: Magnolia Creek Phase 4 (4700 Danube Lane / 1018 Old Evergreen Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's request to rezone 6.71 acres from PDR 4.90 to PDR 7.899 to shift from 13 single-family lots to up to 53 townhouse units (recommended 8-3 by the Planning Commission). In response to Jillian Johnson and Steve Schewel, Planning Director Pat Young and City Attorney Kim Rehberg confirmed the remainder parcel still complied with original 2003 density limits and discussed Commissioner Baker's urban design proposals for the Comprehensive Plan update. Edens proffered $1,000 to Durham Public Schools and $7,950 to the Affordable Housing Fund, and reassured neighbor Giselle Feiger that a 100-foot riparian stream buffer plus 10-foot no-build setback would preserve trees behind Old Evergreen Drive; Council passed the consistency statement and rezoning 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: All Saints United Methodist Church (116 & 120 Smallwood Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Tim Sivers's request for utility extension, voluntary contiguous annexation, and Rural Residential translation for 11.27 acres owned by All Saints United Methodist Church so the church can move off well and septic (noted as revenue negative because the church is tax-exempt). Sivers confirmed to Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson that there were no expansion plans for the vacant acreage beyond connecting to water and future sewer. Council approved annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: 5510 Barbee Chapel Road (International Montessori School & Soccer Club)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Angela Bailey's request for utility extension, voluntary annexation, and Rural Residential/Falls Jordan District B translation on 38.51 acres at 5510 Barbee Chapel Road for a proposed educational facility and soccer club (revenue negative as a nonprofit). Council questioned staff and the applicant regarding the former church site and soccer club use before approving annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Huntington Valley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a consolidated annexation for Huntington Valley, where staff noted a common-ownership plat could be reconfigured from 102 lots to 90 lots (10,000–20,000 sq ft each), avoiding the ordinance's second-access requirement triggered above 90 lots. Applicant representative Robert Schunk explained floodway constraints on the southern half already in city limits and noted builders sought homes below $300,000 without rezoning; Jamie Sunyak clarified no affordable housing proffers could be accepted without a development plan. Council approved annexation, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Hopewell Academy (4651 Comstock Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Chad Abbott's request on behalf of RTP International Education LLC to annex 47.707 acres at 4651 Comstock Road with Industrial Light zoning for a 75,000-sq-ft school building, 200-bed dormitory, and soccer field. Council Members questioned the mismatch between Hopewell Academy's nonprofit status and the staff report's revenue-positive for-profit finding until Head of School Randy Taylor arrived late and explained that for-profit parent RTP International Education LLC was building the facility to lease to the nonprofit school, and builder Steve Hubrich noted $350,000–$400,000 in impact fees; resident Aker Medina urged tuition scholarships for nearby students. Weighing staff's warning that deferral past September 30 would delay annexation effectiveness until December 31, Council approved annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 16, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the livestream recording of the September 16, 2019 Durham City Council meeting, four members—Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero—convened and voted 4-0 to grant excused absences to ill Council Members Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman (with Mark-Anthony Middleton already excused). After six ceremonial proclamations including the Sibiu, Romania Sister City partnership and Neighbor Spotlight Marcella Thompson, Council voted 4-0 in open session to approve annual performance-review salaries for City Clerk Diana Schreiber ($97,335) and City Manager Tom Bonfield ($255,191). Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda 4-0 (excluding pulled Items 19 and 20) and subsequently passed pulled Item 19 (MS4 stormwater inspections) and Item 20 (Alleyway 13 stormwater repairs) 4-0. Council then held six consolidated annexation and rezoning public hearings—New Haven Townhouses (Item 23), Magnolia Creek Phase 4 (Item 24), All Saints United Methodist Church (Item 25), 5510 Barbee Chapel Road (Item 26), Huntington Valley (Item 27), and Hopewell Academy (Item 28)—and approved every motion unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absences for Council Members Alston and Freeman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed four members present: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero. Council voted 4-0 to grant excused absences to ill Council Members Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman, noting Mark-Anthony Middleton's previously granted excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Sibiu Sister City Agreement, Hunger/Preparedness Proclamations, Neighbor Spotlight, and Early Voting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council hosted a Sister City proclamation with Sibiu, Romania, recognized Senior Hunger Awareness Week, Hunger Free Durham Month, Diaper Need Awareness Week, and National Preparedness Month, heard historian Eddie Davis honor Sam Reed, and presented the Neighbor Spotlight to Marcella Thompson. Charlie Reece reminded residents that two weeks of early voting for the October 8 primary opened September 18.

agenda_items.title: Approval of City Clerk and City Manager Salaries Following Annual Performance Reviews
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel announced that Council completed positive closed-session evaluations for City Clerk Diana Schreiber and City Manager Tom Bonfield and required an open-session vote on their salaries. Council voted 4-0 to approve salaries with raises of $97,335 for the City Clerk and $255,191 for the City Manager.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 19 and 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager's office, City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items. Charlie Reece pulled Item 19 for a brief comment under a point of order, and resident Mr. Andrews pulled Item 20. Remaining consent items covering appointments, Community Safety Task Force discussion, Affordable Housing Bond Advisory Committee report, rapid rehousing amendment, electric buses, Cornwallis Road sidewalks, and stormwater/drainage contracts passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Inspections Contracts (SD-2019-06 & SD-2019-07)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece explained that staff verified no subcontracting opportunities existed for the specialized MS4 inspections and no certified MWBE vendors in the city's database perform that work. He moved approval so critical stormwater inspections could proceed, passing 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Infrastructure Repairs SD-2019-02 Amendment #2 (Alleyway 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Mr. Andrews spoke in support of fixing sinkholes on Alleyway 13 while urging the city to address 35 acres of impervious Duke campus runoff overwhelming the 100-year-old 24-inch pipe near Buchanan Boulevard. Public Works staffer Dana Hornkohl acknowledged legacy drainage issues and agreed to meet with Andrews regarding regional stormwater planning; Council approved the amendment 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Item: New Haven Townhouses (2600 Ellis Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's FLUM amendment and rezoning from RS-20 to PDR 6.239 for up to 55 townhouses on 9.116 acres at 2600 Ellis Road (recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission). Edens proffered $8,250 to Durham's Affordable Housing Fund, and Council adopted the FLUM amendment, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Zoning Map Change: Magnolia Creek Phase 4 (4700 Danube Lane / 1018 Old Evergreen Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's rezoning of 6.71 acres from PDR 4.90 to PDR 7.899 for up to 53 townhouse units (recommended 8-3 by the Planning Commission). Pat Young and Kim Rehberg addressed density calculation questions on the remainder tract, Edens proffered $1,000 to DPS and $7,950 to the Affordable Housing Fund, and staff confirmed to resident Giselle Feiger that a 100-foot riparian buffer would remain behind Old Evergreen Drive; Council passed the consistency statement and rezoning 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: All Saints United Methodist Church (116 & 120 Smallwood Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Tim Sivers's utility extension, voluntary annexation, and Rural Residential translation for 11.27 acres owned by All Saints United Methodist Church to connect to city water. Sivers confirmed to Jillian Johnson that no expansion was planned on the vacant land; Council adopted annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: 5510 Barbee Chapel Road (International Montessori School & Soccer Club)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Angela Bailey's utility extension, annexation, and Rural Residential / Falls Jordan District B zoning translation for 38.51 acres at 5510 Barbee Chapel Road for an educational facility and soccer club. Following Council questions on the site's former church use and operations, Council passed annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Huntington Valley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and applicant representative Robert Schunk explained the Huntington Valley annexation would allow replatting to 90 single-family lots (at the 90-lot single-access threshold) on the northern half above floodplains, targeting homes below $300,000 without rezoning or proffers. Council approved annexation, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Hopewell Academy (4651 Comstock Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Chad Abbott's annexation and Industrial Light zoning request for 47.707 acres at 4651 Comstock Road on behalf of RTP International Education LLC for a school building, 200-bed dormitory, and soccer field. Council questioned the relationship between nonprofit Hopewell Academy and for-profit parent RTP International Education LLC until Head of School Randy Taylor and builder Steve Hubrich clarified the lease/investment structure and $350,000–$400,000 in impact fees, while resident Aker Medina requested tuition scholarships for local students. Council approved annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 3, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly five-hour session on September 3, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council recognized South Durham Little League champions, RBI baseball, National Recovery Month, and Hurricane Dorian emergency shelter preparations before approving the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 12 and 15). Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report—noting a 16% rise in Part 1 violent crime (including 21 homicides and 312 shooting incidents), robberies targeting Hispanic residents, and a 5.8-minute Priority 1 response time—followed by Jason Schiess's traffic stop data presentation and intense public comment on gun violence and police staffing. Council then passed pulled Item 12 (Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations design) and Item 15 ($1.5M sidewalk repairs contract SW-67) 7-0. After an extensive public hearing on Item 17, Expanding Housing Choices (EHC), Council passed both the statutory consistency statement and the UDO text amendment allowing duplexes, accessory dwelling units, small-lot options, and flag lots in the urban tier by 6-1 split votes—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting No over source-of-income protections, unrelated-resident rules, and displacement concerns—before unanimously approving a metrics reporting resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Youth Baseball & Recovery Proclamations, and Hurricane Dorian Shelter Prep
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Council honored the South Durham Little League 7–8-year-old Orange All-Star state champions, the RBI baseball program, National Recovery Month (announcing a September 14 Durham Central Park event), and local muralists, and received an emergency management briefing on Hurricane Dorian sheltering with DPD hourly presence and a Charlotte-area ambulance strike team.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 12 and 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk and administration presented no priority items. Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering minutes, board and Civilian Police Review Board appointments, 2020 council schedule, GoDurham transit advertising policy, Carpenter Fletcher and Hillandale sidewalk/bike-lane agreements, NLC Leadership and Community Resilience grant, and USGS rainfall/streamflow monitoring. With Items 12 and 15 pulled by Victoria Peterson, Council adopted the Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report and Six-Month Traffic Stop Data Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported that Q1–Q2 Part 1 violent crime rose 16% (21 homicides, 312 shooting incidents, and 44% of person robberies involving Hispanic victims, later easing in Q3), while burglaries hit a 10-year low, Priority 1 response times hit the 5.8-minute target, and sworn staffing reached 96% (98% with BLET 50). Jason Schiess presented SBI-122 traffic stop data showing 7,616 stops (+14% YoY but under half of 2010 levels), a 1.0 RTI veil-of-darkness risk ratio, higher search rates for Black drivers (8.67%) alongside no enforcement action in 61% of stops of Black drivers, and a record 51% probable-cause contraband hit rate. During public comment, Chris Tiffany, Jackie Wagstaff, Shea Ramirez, Cheryl Smith, Dennis Garrett, Rafael Zayidi, and Victoria Peterson clashed with Council over gun violence, shuttered recreation centers, and police officer funding.

agenda_items.title: Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 12 to urge Council to use fund balance reserves to reopen and expand community recreation centers and senior programming near McDougald Terrace. Council approved the Vines Architecture design services contract for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 ($1.5 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson briefly commented on needing stronger zoning and property building standards after pulling Item 15. Council moved, seconded, and approved Contract SW-67 for approximately $1.5 million in sidewalk repairs 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young presented the 15-month Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) text amendment to allow duplexes across urban-tier residential districts, expand 800-sq-ft ADUs, add a 2,000-sq-ft small-lot option and narrow flag lots, remove minimum lot-width infill rules, and allow duplexes/townhouses in suburban cluster subdivisions, noting single-family zoning's redlining legacy. Following lengthy public testimony, Mark-Anthony Middleton supported EHC with a request for six-month monitoring to prevent 'gentrification on steroids,' Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, and Charlie Reece backed immediate adoption without the Planning Commission's 12-month delay or historic-district exemption, and DeDreana Freeman opposed immediate passage citing missing source-of-income protections and unresolved unrelated-occupant rules. Council passed the consistency statement 6-1, the UDO text amendment 6-1, and a metrics monitoring resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13, and 14, excluding pulled Items 12 and 15)
votes.discussion_detail: With Items 12 and 15 pulled by Victoria Peterson, Council unanimously approved the remaining Consent Agenda items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12 — Approve Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
votes.discussion_detail: Following remarks by Victoria Peterson advocating additional recreation and senior facilities near McDougald Terrace, Council approved the design services contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 (~$1.5 Million)
votes.discussion_detail: After brief public comment from Victoria Peterson, Council unanimously approved sidewalk repair Contract SW-67 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Statutory Consistency Statement for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Following nearly two and a half hours of presentation, public hearing testimony, and council debate, Council adopted the consistency statement for Expanding Housing Choices 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Ordinance Amending Unified Development Ordinance for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment 6-1, legalizing duplexes, expanded ADUs, 2,000-sq-ft small lots, and narrow flag lots in urban-tier residential districts; DeDreana Freeman voted No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Resolution Regarding Development and Reporting of Metrics for Expanding Housing Choices
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted a companion resolution directing staff to develop and report monitoring metrics on the impacts of Expanding Housing Choices 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment Timing, Equity Safeguards, and Displacement Risk (Item 17)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to immediately enact the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment across all urban-tier neighborhoods or delay implementation for 12 months until the Comprehensive Plan update and stronger tenant/equity protections were in place, passing the ordinance 6-1.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Expanding Housing Choices immediately across the urban tier (including historic districts) alongside ongoing metrics monitoring and the $95 million housing bond.
side_a_arguments: Single-family-only zoning perpetuates historical redlining and drives up prices in lower-income neighborhoods by restricting supply in high-demand areas.

Tear-downs for large luxury single-family homes are already occurring under existing rules; EHC enables incremental gentle density, small-lot homes, and ADUs that help market-rate filtering and homeowner equity.
Exempting local historic districts or delaying 12 months would perpetuate systemic inequity and stall needed housing supply after 15 months of community engagement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose passing the amendment now without source-of-income voucher protections, unrelated-resident occupancy reforms, and waiting for the Comprehensive Plan.
side_b_arguments: Waiting 12 months for the Comprehensive Plan update would allow broader alignment rather than rushing a complex zoning overhaul.
The proposal lacks protections against Section 8 source-of-income discrimination and omits reforms to the three-unrelated-residents occupancy limit.
Removing single-family zoning without direct equity investments risks speculative developer activity in historic middle-class neighborhoods of color without guaranteeing affordable units.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and EHC UDO text amendment passed 6-1 (DeDreana Freeman voting No), followed by a unanimous 7-0 vote on the metrics monitoring resolution.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 3, 2019 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: In the closed-captioned broadcast of the September 3, 2019 Durham City Council meeting with all seven members present, Council celebrated South Durham Little League champions, RBI baseball, National Recovery Month, and Hurricane Dorian preparedness before adopting the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 12 and 15). Police Chief C.J. Davis delivered the 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report—highlighting a 16% increase in Part 1 violent crime (including 21 homicides and 312 shooting incidents) alongside a 10-year low in burglaries and a 5.8-minute Priority 1 response time—followed by Jason Schiess's traffic stop report and public comments regarding gun violence and officer staffing. Council approved pulled Item 12 (Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center design) and Item 15 ($1.5M sidewalk repair Contract SW-67) 7-0. Concluding a lengthy public hearing on Item 17, Expanding Housing Choices (EHC), Council passed the consistency statement and UDO text amendment 6-1—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting No—and unanimously passed a metrics reporting resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Youth Baseball & Recovery Proclamations, and Hurricane Dorian Shelter Prep
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven council members attended. Council recognized the South Durham Little League 7–8-year-old Orange All-Star state champions, RBI baseball, National Recovery Month (September 14 event at Durham Central Park), and local muralists, and heard an emergency shelter briefing for Hurricane Dorian.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 12 and 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk and administration reported no priority items. Mayor Schewel read Consent Agenda Items 1–15 covering minutes, appointments, 2020 council schedule, GoDurham transit advertising policy, Carpenter Fletcher and Hillandale sidewalk/bike-lane agreements, NLC resilience grant, and USGS rainfall/streamflow monitoring. Excluding Items 12 and 15 pulled by Victoria Peterson, Council approved the Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report and Six-Month Traffic Stop Data Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported Q1–Q2 Part 1 violent crime rose 16% (21 criminal homicides, 312 shootings, 415 illegal guns seized, and heightened robberies of Hispanic residents), while burglaries fell to a 10-year low and Priority 1 response times met the 5.8-minute target. Jason Schiess presented SBI-122 traffic stop data showing 7,616 stops (+14% YoY), a 1.0 RTI veil-of-darkness risk ratio, an 8.67% search rate for Black drivers with no enforcement action in 61% of stops, and a 51% probable-cause contraband hit rate, followed by sharp public comment on gun violence and police funding.

agenda_items.title: Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 12 to call for greater investment from fund balance reserves in recreation centers and senior programs near McDougald Terrace. Council approved the Vines Architecture design contract for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 ($1.5 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 15 and offered brief remarks urging better zoning and development standards. Council unanimously approved sidewalk repair Contract SW-67 for approximately $1.5 million by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young presented the Expanding Housing Choices text amendment enabling duplexes across urban-tier residential districts, expanded 800-sq-ft ADUs, 2,000-sq-ft small lots, narrow flag lots, and suburban cluster duplexes/townhomes. After extensive public testimony, Mark-Anthony Middleton backed EHC with six-month monitoring, Mayor Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, and Charlie Reece supported immediate passage without exempting historic districts, and DeDreana Freeman voted No citing missing Section 8 source-of-income protections and unresolved occupancy limits. Council approved the consistency statement and UDO amendment 6-1, and passed the metrics reporting resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13, and 14, excluding pulled Items 12 and 15)
votes.discussion_detail: Excluding pulled Items 12 and 15, Council unanimously adopted the Consent Agenda 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12 — Approve Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
votes.discussion_detail: After public comment by Victoria Peterson, Council approved the design services contract for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 (~$1.5 Million)
votes.discussion_detail: Following brief remarks by Victoria Peterson, Council approved Contract SW-67 sidewalk repairs 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Statutory Consistency Statement for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consistency statement for the Expanding Housing Choices text amendment 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Ordinance Amending Unified Development Ordinance for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Resolution Regarding Development and Reporting of Metrics for Expanding Housing Choices
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the resolution directing development and periodic reporting of Expanding Housing Choices metrics 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Sept 3, 2019 (with closed captions)
disagreements.issue: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment Timing, Equity Safeguards, and Displacement Risk (Item 17)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to enact Expanding Housing Choices immediately across the urban tier or delay implementation 12 months pending the Comprehensive Plan and stronger equity/tenant protections, adopting the ordinance 6-1.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Expanding Housing Choices immediately across urban-tier districts (including historic districts) paired with monitoring and the $95 million housing bond.
side_a_arguments: Single-family zoning reflects historical redlining and pushes displacement into lower-income neighborhoods.
Gentle infill housing choices (duplexes, ADUs, small lots) slow price escalation and support small homeowners and developers.
Delaying 12 months or exempting historic districts would perpetuate systemic inequity after 15 months of public engagement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose immediate passage without source-of-income voucher protections, unrelated-occupant rule changes, and Comprehensive Plan integration.
side_b_arguments: The ordinance moves ahead of the Comprehensive Plan update without binding affordable housing or source-of-income protections.
Reforms to the unrelated-residents limit and anti-displacement investments should be addressed before opening neighborhoods to speculative development.
disagreements.resolution: Consistency statement and UDO text amendment passed 6-1 (DeDreana Freeman voting No), while the monitoring metrics resolution passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 19, 2019 (Live stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Opening on August 19, 2019 with all seven members present, Mayor Steve Schewel mourned public health pioneer Dr. Evelyn Schmidt and 9-year-old shooting victim Zion Person, prompting Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman to challenge Council to adopt concrete emergency gun-violence measures or mid-cycle appropriations. Council also celebrated a Sister City partnership with Celaya, Mexico and approved the City Manager's priority item referring the Oregon Street closing (Item 16) back to administration 7-0, before adopting the Consent Agenda 7-0 (including sidewalk supplemental agreements, an NLC fines-and-fees grant, Twin Lakes Park easement sale, and Durham County recycling). In the meeting's sole public hearing (Item 17), Council conducted a quasi-judicial hearing for Towerview Business Center's 60% Major Transportation Corridor buffer reduction (from 100 feet to 40 feet along the I-40 Page Road off-ramp) and associated 12,452-square-foot office building site plan at 4804 Page Creek Lane, voting 7-0 across three motions to open evidence, grant Major Special Use Permit M1800002, and approve Major Site Plan D1800246.

agenda_items.title: Tributes to Dr. Evelyn Schmidt & Zion Person, Celaya Sister City Agreement, and Gun Violence Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened with remarks mourning Dr. Evelyn Schmidt and 9-year-old shooting victim Zion Person, calling for gun-control action and youth/mental-health supports, while congratulating Chief C.J. Davis on becoming president of NOBLE. Council celebrated a Sister City agreement with Celaya, Mexico, and Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman delivered impassioned remarks after speaking with Zion Person's aunt—challenging colleagues to put Durham on emergency footing and approve concrete anti-violence appropriations or Durham Beyond Policing initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Item (Refer Item 16 Back), Boards/Commissions Video, and Consent Agenda (Items 1-13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented one priority item referring Item 16 (Oregon Street closing) back to the administration at the petitioner's request, which Council approved 7-0. The City Clerk debuted a new recruitment video for Durham's nearly 30 boards, committees, and commissions, and Council unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items 1–13 (covering appointments, NLC equitable fines-and-fees grant, LaSalle/Raynor/N. Duke Street sidewalk agreements, Twin Lakes Park easement, NRPA grant, Durham County recycling amendment, and CityWorks upgrade) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — Towerview Business Center MTC-40 Buffer Reduction (MSUP M1800002 & Site Plan D1800246)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Eliza Monroe presented Nelson Partners and Milestone Development LLC's application for a 60% Major Transportation Corridor buffer reduction (from 100 feet to 40 feet) along the I-40 Page Road off-ramp to build a 12,452-sq-ft two-story office building at 4804 Page Creek Lane. Attorney Neil Gosh, originator Carlton Midgett, engineer Bill Daniel, and appraiser Jarvis Martin testified that a 1998 NCDOT condemnation took 1.3 acres and slid the 100-foot buffer onto the narrow lot, making it undevelopable, while the adjacent hotel already held a 40-foot buffer and property values would not be harmed. With no opponents appearing and staff recommending approval, Council voted 7-0 to conduct the hearing and admit evidence, 7-0 to grant MSUP M1800002, and 7-0 to approve Major Site Plan D1800246, before Mayor Schewel urged Planning Director Pat Young to continue reviewing which special use permits could be handled administratively or legislatively.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Item — Refer Item 16 (Oregon Street Closing Public Hearing) Back to Administration
votes.discussion_detail: At the request of the petitioner, Council voted 7-0 to accept the City Manager's priority item referring Item 16 (Oregon Street closing) back to the administration.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Motion to Conduct Quasi-Judicial Public Hearing and Receive Evidence (Towerview Business Center M1800002)
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 7-0 to formally conduct the quasi-judicial public hearing and receive evidence for Major Special Use Permit M1800002.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Grant Major Special Use Permit M1800002 (Towerview Business Center MTC 40-Foot Buffer Reduction)
votes.discussion_detail: Following uncontested expert testimony on NCDOT condemnation hardship, highway off-ramp visibility, vegetation screening, and adjacent hotel precedent, Council granted Major Special Use Permit M1800002 by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Approve Major Site Plan D1800246 (Towerview Business Center)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved associated Major Site Plan D1800246 for the 12,452-sq-ft two-story office building at 4804 Page Creek Lane 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 5, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Returning from summer recess on August 5, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council recognized Cleft and Craniofacial Awareness Month, Love and Respect Ministry, the Hillside Park Basketball Courts award, National Night Out, and the Algonquin Tennis Club state historical marker before confirming Earl Bradley to the Workers' Rights Commission and adopting the Consent Agenda 7-0. In two consecutive quasi-judicial hearings, Council voted 7-0 to grant Major Special Use Permit M1900001 (with a signalization coordination condition) and Site Plan D1800303 for a 105,000-square-foot North Carolina Central University Student Center—after neighbors raised notice and parking concerns—and 7-0 to approve MSUP M1900002 and Site Plan D1800032 for a ready-mix concrete plant at 1435 Camden Avenue. Council then unanimously passed 7-0 across all motions for East Carver Street right-of-way annexation (Item 34), Mist Lake Drive permanent street closing and access easement (Item 35), Cardinal Oaks annexation (Item 36), the landmark Patterson Place Compact Suburban Design District text amendment, rezoning, and street network (Item 37, following a compromise protecting New Hope Creek and prohibiting payday lenders), and service area fees for the Andrews Chapel lift station (Item 38) and Copley Farm sewer outfall (Item 39).

agenda_items.title: Proclamations, Hillside Park Award, and Workers' Rights Commission Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the post-recess meeting to order with all seven members present. Council presented proclamations for Cleft and Craniofacial Awareness Month (with Duke's Dr. Jeffrey Marcus), Love and Respect Ministry (Dennis Garrett), National Night Out, and the Algonquin Tennis Club's upcoming state historical marker, plus the APA-NC Great Places People's Choice Award for Hillside Park Basketball Courts. Council approved the City Clerk's priority appointment of Earl Bradley to the Workers' Rights Commission 7-0 and swore him in.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering minutes, Workers' Rights Commission appointment, June 2019 travel performance audit, GARE Welcome Home grant, NCDOT and FTA transit planning grants, Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge agreement with Duke, MPO web applications, NC 54 sidewalk and Safe Routes to School agreements, water supply property ordinance, Triangle Water Supply Partnership, Flowers Drive sewer transfer, May/June bid reports, and municipal software contracts. Council adopted the Consent Agenda unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — NCCU Student Center (MSUP M1900001 & Major Site Plan D1800303)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Eliza Monroe presented North Carolina Central University's request for a Major Special Use Permit and Major Site Plan to construct a 2.5-story, 105,000-sq-ft student center replacing a 228-space parking lot with 110 spaces on campus. Nearby residents Reinhard Kelly, Charles Kelly, Ronald McCoy, and Jillian Riley testified about short quasi-judicial notice, student overflow parking on Cecil Street, and event traffic, urging a delay, while NCCU counsel Bill Bryan and witnesses defended UDO parking compliance and campus transit plans. Council added a staff-endorsed signalization coordination condition, asked staff to review notice periods and facilitate neighbor-university talks, and approved MSUP M1900001 and Site Plan D1800303 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — 1435 Camden Avenue Concrete Manufacturing Plant (MSUP M1900002 & Site Plan D1800032)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Danny Cultra presented WJD Holdings LLC and Raleigh Concrete LLC's application for a ready-mix concrete plant on 10.058 industrial acres at 1435 Camden Avenue, noting the Board of Adjustment previously granted variances from the 1,500-foot residential separation and major-thoroughfare access rules (B180008) because nearby residential parcels lie in floodway and Camden Avenue already carries industrial traffic. Property owner Dan Wall, plant manager Tim Brown, engineer Dan Papst, traffic engineer, and appraiser Jarvis Martin testified on impervious surface reduction (74% to ~70%), stormwater BMPs, Level of Service C traffic, and property values, with no opponents speaking. Council approved MSUP M1900002 and Site Plan D1800032 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: East Carver Street Right-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented a Public Works voluntary annexation and RS-20 zoning translation for a 10.18-acre portion of East Carver Street right-of-way between Danube Lane and Club Creek Road to enable city roadway maintenance upon completion of the Carver Street extension. With no public speakers, Council approved annexation, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 7-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Permanent Closing of Mist Lake Drive Portion (1,336 Linear Feet) & Access Easement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented the city's request to permanently close 1,336 linear feet of Mist Lake Drive south of Camden Avenue for the Water Management facility redevelopment at 1600 Mist Lake Drive, paired with a 60-foot access easement for Energy United Propane LLC and BIG Properties LLC. Council approved the street closing order and the road maintenance and access easement 7-0 across two votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Cardinal Oaks (BDG1900006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Emily Struthers presented Jeff Heath's voluntary annexation and RR / Falls Jordan District B zoning translation for 0.452 acres of Canakeet Drive right-of-way and open space parcels in Cardinal Oaks so the city can assume street maintenance. Council approved annexation, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 7-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Patterson Place Compact Suburban Design District (Text Amendment, Map Change & Street Network)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Lisa Miller presented the continued Patterson Place Compact Suburban Design District package, highlighting post-May revisions that shrank the core subdistrict per Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit feedback, prohibited payday lenders district-wide, and secured Beacon Properties' proffered variable Transitional Use Area (TUA) and construction best practices protecting New Hope Creek. DeDreana Freeman questioned density-bonus reliance and lift-station sewer capacity; speakers Mike Waldroop, Dr. Bob Healy (New Hope Creek Corridor Advisory Committee / Sierra Club), attorney Patrick Byker (Beacon Properties), Reynolds Smith (DOST), and John Kent endorsed the compromise. Council passed all five motions—text-amendment consistency, text amendment, map-change consistency, map change, and future street network resolution—unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Andrews Chapel Lift Station Service Area and Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner of Public Works presented an ordinance establishing the associated service area and fees for the Andrews Chapel lift station. With no public comments, Council adopted the ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Copley Farm Sanitary Sewer Outfall Service Area and Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner of Public Works presented an ordinance setting the associated service area and fees for the Copley Farm sanitary sewer outfall. With no questions or public speakers, Council adopted the ordinance 7-0 before adjourning at 1:00 a.m.

votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the City Clerk's priority appointment of Earl Bradley to the Workers' Rights Commission 7-0, and the Clerk swore him in.

votes.discussion_detail: Following testimony from NCCU and Cecil Street neighbors regarding notice and parking, Council granted MSUP M1900001 with staff's recommended conditions plus signalization coordination 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 33 — Grant Major Special Use Permit M1900002 (1435 Camden Avenue Concrete Manufacturing Plant)
votes.discussion_detail: With no opponents and full expert evidence addressing UDO findings, prior Board of Adjustment variances, traffic, and property values, Council granted MSUP M1900002 by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 33 — Approve Major Site Plan D1800032 (1435 Camden Avenue Concrete Manufacturing Plant)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved Major Site Plan D1800032 for the 1435 Camden Avenue concrete plant 7-0.

votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the annexation ordinance for East Carver Street right-of-way 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 34 — Adopt Consistency Statement for East Carver Street Right-of-Way
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consistency statement for East Carver Street right-of-way 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 34 — Adopt Ordinance Amending UDO for East Carver Street Right-of-Way (RS-20)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the initial RS-20 zoning ordinance for East Carver Street right-of-way 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 35 — Adopt Order Permanently Closing 1,336 Linear Feet of Mist Lake Drive
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the order permanently closing 1,336 linear feet of Mist Lake Drive for the Water Management facility redevelopment 7-0.
