meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 3, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: In the longest meeting in Durham City Council history (over six hours, adjourning at 1:11 a.m.), Council unanimously referred a Durham County EMS/Fire agreement back to administration 7-0, moved Items 7 and 12 off consent 7-0, and approved the remaining consent slate 7-0 (including reserving public land for housing and the FY18 CAFR). Following a four-hour public hearing pitting transit advocates against Colvard Farms residents and Creekside Elementary parents over noise and environmental concerns, Council voted 7-0 on all four motions to annex and rezone 4901 Farrington Road for GoTriangle's Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Rail Operations Maintenance Facility (ROMF). Council also unanimously approved 7-0 the Weaving Water co-housing annexation, quasi-judicial permits for DPS Elementary School C, Lynnhaven Apartments affordable housing conduit bonds, a $115,000 economic development incentive with Kip Chogay, and privacy revisions to the PARCS parking contract, while adopting the GoTriangle Cooperative Agreement with added DBE language after DeDreana Freeman pressed GoTriangle on equity and transparency. On Item 40 (Christian Avenue street closing), Council passed the closure order 6-1 with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Human Rights/Bill of Rights Proclamation and Priority Agenda Modifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel read a proclamation declaring December 10 and December 15 as Human Rights Day and Bill of Rights Day, highlighting the ICE detention of Durham resident Samuel Oliver-Bruno. Council then approved 7-0 the City Manager's request to refer Item 17 (Durham County EMS/City Fire agreement) back to administration and approved 7-0 the City Attorney's request to move Item 7 (GoTriangle cooperative agreement) and Item 12 (PARCS parking contract privacy language) off consent to the end of the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Reserve Public Land for Housing, HOPWA, Road/Stormwater Contracts, Park Accessibility, CAFR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, covering minutes, boards attendance, cash receipts audit, FY2019-20 budget schedule, a resolution reserving public land for housing, GoTriangle interim reimbursement, HOPWA contracts with DHA and Durham County, NC 751/University Drive bike/pedestrian and Fayetteville Road contracts, CIP budget amendments, sewer inspection trucks, Valley Springs Park accessibility improvements, and the FY2018 CAFR. Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda (excluding Items 7, 12, and 17) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — GoTriangle Rail Operations Maintenance Facility (ROMF, 4901 Farrington Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented GoTriangle's request to annex 53.214 acres, amend the Future Land Use Map to Industrial, and rezone 23.422 acres at 4901 Farrington Road from RS-20 to IL(D) for the Durham-Orange Light Rail ROMF, noting a 4-4 Planning Commission tie and new proffers including 8-foot evergreen buffers, a 4-foot earthen berm, and a ban on site clearing before securing a federal Full Funding Grant Agreement. Nearly 70 speakers (about 19 proponents and 50 opponents, including Colvard Farms residents and Creekside Elementary parents) debated noise (disputing a 136-decibel environmental document figure), chemical/traffic risks, and regional transit needs for four hours. All seven Council members acknowledged neighborhood burdens and pledged strict enforcement of Durham's noise ordinance before approving all four motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Weaving Water Co-Housing (3912 & 3920 Rivermont Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Danielle Resto's request to annex 12.31 acres and rezone from RS-20 to PDR 1.964 for a 24-unit accessible co-housing community of duplexes and triplexes capped at 4,000 square feet per building and 20% impervious surface near Eno River State Park. Applicant Danielle Resto and engineer Katie Hamilton highlighted missing-middle housing ($250,000-$460,000) and green corridor conservation, and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — Durham Public Schools Elementary School C
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a quasi-judicial hearing with sworn testimony presented by attorney Deborah Stagner on behalf of Durham Public Schools for Elementary School C, with no opponents appearing. Following staff recommendations, Council unanimously voted 7-0 to approve the Transportation Special Use Permit (T1600001), Major Special Use Permit (M1800003), and Major Site Plan.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Christian Avenue Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith presented Shane Strickland's (CE Group) request to permanently close a 331-linear-foot portion of Christian Avenue and combine it with adjacent parcels as committed under the Hillsborough/Cole Mill rezoning (C170030). With brief remarks from Mr. Strickland and no opposition speakers, Council approved the street closing order 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds for Lynnhaven Apartments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell and bond counsel Eric Prestel presented a TEFRA reapproval/extension for Public Finance Authority conduit revenue bonds supporting Lynnhaven Apartments off US 70 and Lynn Road, keeping units affordable through 2027 with no city debt liability. Responding to DeDreana Freeman, Mr. Prestel explained rating-agency and HUD delays required reapproval after the prior TEFRA window expired, and Council passed the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Kip Chogay (Kip Ryan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey (OEWD) presented a $115,000 economic development incentive agreement with Kip Chogay (formerly dry-cleaning-remediated site), partnering with Peter Schiller for technical assistance and committing to hire formerly incarcerated workers on construction. Council questioned environmental monitoring and Black Chamber tenant outreach before approving the agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Cooperative Agreement with GoTriangle for D-O LRT Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney presented revised Article 3, Paragraph F language clarifying that final light rail corridor design near Blackwell Street was not yet complete. Council Member DeDreana Freeman criticized GoTriangle's communication and requested staff, board, and DBE contracting diversity data; GoTriangle's John Tallmadge reported staff demographics (35% Black male, 31% Black female, 16% white male, 11% white female, 4% Hispanic male, 2% Hispanic female, 1% multiracial female), and Mayor Schewel added a clause for DBE utilization in future coordination before Council approved the revised motion.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Off-Street Parking Access and Revenue Control System (PARCS) Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney proposed adding privacy language to Section 12(e) of the Carolina Time & Equipment PARCS contract prohibiting the contractor from using vehicle license numbers, vehicle identification numbers, or registration data. DeDreana Freeman thanked staff for strengthening resident privacy protections, and Council approved the contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Item 17 (Durham County EMS / City Fire Agreement) Back to Administration
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved referring Agenda Item 17 back to the administration per the City Manager's priority request.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Ordinance Annexing Rail Operations Maintenance Facility (ROMF) and Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Following a four-hour public hearing and council remarks affirming both support for light rail and strict noise enforcement, Council unanimously adopted the annexation ordinance effective December 31, 2018.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Resolution Amending Future Land Use Map for ROMF (Office/Commercial to Industrial)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously amended the Future Land Use Map designation at 4901 Farrington Road to Industrial.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Consistency Statement for GoTriangle ROMF Zoning Map Change
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the comprehensive plan consistency statement for the ROMF rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Ordinance Amending the UDO for GoTriangle ROMF (RS-20 to IL-D)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved rezoning 23.422 acres at 4901 Farrington Road to Industrial Light with a Development Plan for GoTriangle's light rail maintenance facility.

votes.item_title: Item 38: Ordinance Annexing Weaving Water (3912 & 3920 Rivermont Road) and Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved annexing the 12.31-acre Weaving Water co-housing parcels.

votes.item_title: Item 38: Consistency Statement for Weaving Water
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for Weaving Water.

votes.item_title: Item 38: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Weaving Water (RS-20 to PDR 1.964)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved PDR 1.964 zoning for the 24-unit Weaving Water co-housing community.

votes.item_title: Item 39: Order Approving Transportation Special Use Permit (T1600001) for DPS Elementary School C
votes.discussion_detail: Based on unopposed competent evidence in the quasi-judicial hearing, Council approved the Transportation Special Use Permit 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 39: Order Approving Major Special Use Permit (M1800003) for DPS Elementary School C
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the Major Special Use Permit for DPS Elementary School C.

votes.item_title: Item 39: Approval of Major Site Plan for DPS Elementary School C
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the non-quasi-judicial Major Site Plan for DPS Elementary School C.

votes.item_title: Item 40: Order Permanently Closing a 331-Linear-Foot Portion of Christian Avenue
votes.discussion_detail: Following Grace Smith's presentation of the street closing committed under zoning case C170030, Council passed the closure order 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 41: Resolution Approving Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds for Lynnhaven Apartments
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously reapproved the TEFRA conduit bond resolution for Lynnhaven Apartments.

votes.item_title: Item 42: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Kip Chogay ($115,000)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously authorized the $115,000 economic development incentive agreement with Kip Chogay.

votes.item_title: Item 7: Resolution Ratifying Cooperative Agreement with GoTriangle (with Revised Article 3, Paragraph F and DBE Clause)
votes.notes: Numeric tally not spoken aloud on the audio recording when vote closed at 06:10:46.
votes.discussion_detail: Following debate over GoTriangle's communication, equity planning, and DBE/workforce statistics, Council voted on the revised resolution incorporating Article 3(F) changes and DBE utilization language; the clerk closed the vote and the Mayor thanked Council and proceeded to Item 12 without announcing a numeric tally aloud.

votes.item_title: Item 12: PARCS Off-Street Parking Contract with Carolina Time & Equipment (with Section 12(e) Privacy Revision)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously authorized execution of the PARCS parking contract incorporating added privacy prohibitions on customer vehicle license, VIN, and registration data.

disagreements.issue: Christian Avenue Street Closing (Item 40)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to permanently close a 331-linear-foot portion of Christian Avenue tied to the Hillsborough/Cole Mill rezoning, with DeDreana Freeman casting the sole Nay vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the permanent right-of-way closure as committed under approved zoning case C170030.
side_a_arguments: The closure met all UDO requirements, resolved review agency comments, and was committed as part of the prior Hillsborough/Cole Mill rezoning.
The applicant stated the segment is largely unused and would be combined with adjacent parcels.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose permanently closing the public street right-of-way.
side_b_arguments: Voted Nay without floor remarks (consistent with Freeman's broader skepticism toward vacating public rights-of-way).
disagreements.resolution: Order permanently closing Christian Avenue passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: GoTriangle Community Engagement, Transparency, and Equity Accountability (Items 37 and 7)
disagreements.summary: Although all seven Council members ultimately supported the ROMF rezoning 7-0, DeDreana Freeman strongly criticized GoTriangle's lack of transparency, race-equity planning, and delayed disclosure of DBE and board demographic data, prompting added DBE coordination language in Item 7.
disagreements.side_a_position: Condition future GoTriangle coordination on explicit DBE utilization and hold GoTriangle accountable for race equity and transparency.
side_a_arguments: Obtaining staffing, contracting, and board diversity statistics from GoTriangle felt like 'pulling teeth' and lacked proactive environmental justice and race-equity engagement.
Neighborhood residents and communities of color bear uneven burdens from major transit infrastructure without transparent early engagement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed with both the ROMF rezoning and Cooperative Agreement while acknowledging GoTriangle's recent outreach improvements and substantial minority/women workforce numbers.
side_b_arguments: John Tallmadge reported GoTriangle's workforce is 35% Black male and 31% Black female, which Mayor Schewel praised as substantial.
Light rail is a vital generational investment and Council added DBE coordination language to address Freeman's concern.
disagreements.resolution: ROMF passed 7-0; Item 7 passed with added DBE coordination language.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 19, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 19, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council presented ceremonial proclamations memorializing civic leader Dillard Teer and honoring the Durham Chapter of The Links, recognized DPAC's national and state theater awards and Durham's second-place Digital Cities Survey transparency award, and unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0 (pulling Item 8 for public speakers). Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2018 Third Quarter Crime Report showing a 7% drop in Part 1 index crime and a 17% drop in violent crime alongside 26 year-to-date homicides. Council voted 7-0 to approve the Barbee Road/NC 54 rezoning for up to 112 townhomes (with $5,500 proffered to DPS and $20,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund), held the FY2019-20 Annual Action Needs public hearing for federal HUD grants, voted 7-0 to approve up to $130 million in tax-exempt conduit revenue bonds for North Carolina Central University student housing, and unanimously approved 7-0 the five-year lease for DPD District 3 Substation after hearing community pleas for transparency in the fatal shooting of NCCU student DeAndre Ballard.

agenda_items.title: Dillard Teer Memorial Proclamation, The Links Recognition, Neighbor Spotlight, DPAC & Digital City Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel read proclamations memorializing late Durham civic and construction leader Dillard Teer and honoring the Durham Chapter of The Links Inc., and presented the November Neighbor Spotlight Award to Ms. Burris. Bob Klaus shared DPAC's recognition as IEBA Theater of the Year and NC Visitor Attraction of the Year, and a Council member presented Durham's second-place Digital Cities Survey award for technology-driven transparency.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (DHA/HRC/RAC Appointments, DCLT & Habitat Grants, Water Partnership MOA, EPA Brownfields Grant, Sibiu Sister City)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent slate including minutes, board appointments, a rehabilitation contract with Durham Community Land Trustees at 1700 Merrymac Street, a Habitat for Humanity minor repair contract, the Triangle Water Supply Partnership MOA, Fayetteville Road parcel condemnation, an EPA 2018 Brownfields Assessment Grant, and a Sibiu, Romania sister city proposal. Pulling Item 8 for two registered speakers, Council passed the remaining consent items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2018 Third Quarter Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported that Part 1 index crime fell 7% in the first nine months of 2018 compared to 2017, with violent crime down 17% (three-year lows in robberies and aggravated assaults) and property crime down 5% (18-year low in burglaries), though homicides rose to 26 from 16 in 2017. She also detailed the Park Smart vehicle theft initiative, Priority 1 average response time of 6.03 minutes, 97% sworn staffing, and expanded U-visa certifications for crime victims.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Barbee Road / NC 54 Townhouses (1007 E. NC 54 & 6452 Barbee Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Edens Land's (Jared Edens) request to modify a Commercial General (CG-D) development plan on 14.38 acres from 160,000 square feet of retail to a maximum of 112 townhomes ($200,000-$230,000 expected price points), following a 10-2 Planning Commission recommendation. Mr. Edens proffered $5,500 to Durham Public Schools and $20,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund at first final plan; Council Member Charlie Reece expressed regret for not explaining his lone 6-1 dissent on the earlier retail case and praised the residential shift before Council passed both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — FY 2019-2020 Annual Action Plan Community Development Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reginald Johnson and Wilma Conyers (Community Development) held the first of two required HUD public hearings for the FY2019-20 Annual Action Plan, projecting approximately $1.9 million in CDBG, $1 million in HOME, $160,000 in ESG, and $370,000 in HOPWA funds. Speakers Larissa Sybil, Muna Mujahid, and Jarvis Martin urged preserving expiring affordable housing units and creating housing near transit, while DeDreana Freeman emphasized raising incomes for Black and Latino residents.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Revenue Bonds for North Carolina Central University Student Housing Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd presented a federal TEFRA public hearing for tax-exempt conduit revenue bonds up to $130 million issued by the Arizona Industrial Development Authority for NCCU student housing, noting the City bears no debt liability. NCCU representative Akua Matherson appeared for questions, and Council unanimously adopted the approval resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Five-Year Lease for Durham Police Department District 3 Substation (10 Consultant Place)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Reginald Thompson (NCCU grad student) and Trevor Wells voiced support for the District 3 substation lease but demanded justice and faster investigative transparency in the shooting death of NCCU senior DeAndre Ballard. Mayor Schewel explained the City was awaiting SBI lab results and suggested with Vernetta Alston adding state crime lab funding to the legislative agenda, while DeDreana Freeman floated a letter to the Governor before Council approved the lease 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3-7, 10, 12-14, excluding pulled Item 8)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding Item 8, which was held for registered public speakers.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Consistency Statement for Barbee Road / NC 54 Townhouses (1007 E. NC 54 & 6452 Barbee Road)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement after Charlie Reece and DeDreana Freeman voiced support for shifting the site from retail to 112 townhomes.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Barbee Road / NC 54 Townhouses (CG-D)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the CG-D development plan change permitting up to 112 townhomes with $5,500 proffered to DPS and $20,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Resolution Approving Student Housing Revenue Bonds for North Carolina Central University Project (up to $130M)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the federal TEFRA hearing, Council unanimously approved the conduit bond resolution for NCCU student housing.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Authorize City Manager to Execute Five-Year Lease for DPD District 3 Substation (10 Consultant Place)
votes.discussion_detail: After hearing public testimony regarding the DeAndre Ballard investigation and discussing state crime lab funding delays, Council unanimously approved the District 3 substation lease 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 8, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: Rescheduled to Thursday afternoon November 8, 2018 following a Monday night electrical grid outage, the Durham City Council convened with a four-member quorum (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Vernetta Alston) and voted 4-0 to excuse Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Mark-Anthony Middleton, who were attending the National League of Cities convention. Council proclaimed November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day for the World War I Armistice centennial alongside Veterans Administration staff, added and passed 4-0 an ordinance formally establishing fare-free transit on Election Day (November 6), and approved the consent agenda 4-0. Council also voted 4-0 to permanently close a 1,579-linear-foot portion of Johnson Victory Circle and passed 4-0 two pulled consent transit items—a $492,598 FTA Section 5310 grant for seniors and riders with disabilities and an NCDOT/County Community Connectivity Plan interlocal agreement—after speaker Chris Tiffany criticized upstairs work sessions as insufficiently transparent.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Rescheduling Note, and Excusal of Absent Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel noted the meeting was rescheduled from Monday night due to a power outage and confirmed with the Clerk that four members constituted a valid quorum. Council voted 4-0 to excuse Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Mark-Anthony Middleton from both the regular meeting and following work session while attending the National League of Cities convention.

agenda_items.title: Bells Across Durham Day Proclamation (WWI Centennial and Veterans Day)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel proclaimed November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day, calling for simultaneous 11-bell ringings at 11:00 a.m. to honor military veterans and peaceful conflict resolution. Eddie Davis and Dr. Christine Imler of the Durham VA Health Care System highlighted local VA partnerships with Duke, NCCU, UNC, ECU, and NC State.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Item — Add Ordinance Establishing Fare-Free Day on Election Day (Tuesday, Nov 6, 2018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Deputy City Manager requested adding supplemental Item 20 establishing a fare-free transit day on Election Day (Tuesday, November 6, 2018), which Council added to the agenda 4-0. Later at 00:25:28, Mayor Schewel praised the administration's Election Day voter transit initiative and Council formally adopted the ordinance 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Appointments, CoC Grant, Wayfinding Design, Bid Report, Refuse/Sewer Trucks, Alston Ave Condemnations, Celaya Sister City, HUD Fair Housing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read consent items covering minutes, BPAC and DCVB appointments, 2018 inventory audit, FY16 Continuum of Care planning grant, Downtown Durham Wayfinding design, September 2018 bid report, five refuse trucks, three sewer vacuum jetter trucks, South Alston Avenue sidewalk condemnations, USGS urban stream study, Celaya Mexico sister city proposal, and HUD fair housing funding. Items 7 and 8 were pulled by a resident, and the remaining consent slate passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Johnson Victory Circle Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith presented Robert Schonk's (Stewart Inc.) request to permanently close 1,579 linear feet of Johnson Victory Circle for recombination with adjacent parcels per Park at Southpoint II zoning case Z170036. With no speakers in opposition, Council approved the permanent closure order 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — FY17 & FY18 FTA Section 5310 Grant Project Ordinance ($492,598)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Chris Tiffany pulled Items 7 and 8, alleging that upstairs Council work sessions lack live-streaming and transparency and accusing transit planning of gentrifying Durham. Council approved the $492,598 FTA Section 5310 grant supporting transit for seniors and individuals with disabilities 4-0 (and reminded Mr. Tiffany at adjournment that work sessions are open to the public).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Interlocal Agreement for Durham Coordinated Systems Community Connectivity Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Chris Tiffany's earlier comments, Council considered the interlocal agreement among NCDOT, the City of Durham, and Durham County for the Durham Coordinated Systems Community Connectivity Plan and approved it 4-0.

agenda_items.title: FEMA and SBA Disaster Assistance Information
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Information Officer Corey Williams briefed residents and business owners on available FEMA grants and SBA low-interest disaster assistance loans following recent storms before Council adjourned at 1:37 p.m. to its work session.

votes.item_title: Excuse Council Members Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Mark-Anthony Middleton (National League of Cities)
votes.notes: Caballero, Freeman, and Middleton excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: The four present members voted unanimously 4-0 to excuse Caballero, Freeman, and Middleton from the Nov. 8 meeting and subsequent work session.

votes.item_title: Add Manager's Priority Item 20 (Ordinance Establishing Fare-Free Day on November 6, 2018)
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 4-0 to add Item 20 to the meeting agenda per the Deputy City Manager's request.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-6, 9-15, 19, excluding pulled Items 7 and 8)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda minus Items 7 and 8, which were pulled by resident Chris Tiffany.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Order Permanently Closing 1,579 Linear Feet of Johnson Victory Circle
votes.discussion_detail: Following Grace Smith's presentation and no public speakers, Council passed the street closing order 4-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Establishing Fare-Free Bus Day on Tuesday, November 6, 2018
votes.discussion_detail: Council formally adopted the ordinance ratifying fare-free Election Day bus service 4-0.

votes.item_title: Item 7: FY17 & FY18 FTA Section 5310 Grant Project Ordinance ($492,598)
votes.discussion_detail: Following public remarks from Chris Tiffany, Council voted 4-0 to approve the $492,598 FTA Section 5310 grant supporting senior and disability riders.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Interlocal Agreement with NCDOT and Durham County for Durham Coordinated Systems Community Connectivity Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the interlocal connectivity plan agreement 4-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 15, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 15, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council proclaimed Indigenous Peoples Day, honored Neighbor Spotlight recipient Victor Velazquez Luna, recognized Duke Energy storm restoration crews and late civic leader Dillard Teer, and unanimously voted 7-0 to approve annual raises for the City Manager ($243,503), City Attorney ($223,982), and City Clerk ($92,700). Council unanimously approved the consent agenda (excluding pulled Items 4, 5, and 6) and voted 7-0 to rezone 619 Herndon Road to RS-20 for a fire station. Council approved a $750,000 rehabilitation grant to Durham Community Land Trustees (Item 4) 7-0 after Victoria Peterson urged paid construction job training for young Black men, and voted 7-0 to follow staff's recommendation denying Revial LLC's request to extend expired 2005 street impact fee credits for the Park at Southpoint auto park (Item 5). Finally, Council approved 7-0 an ordinance establishing permitting regulations for shared active transportation companies (Item 6) while pressing Bird representative Servando Esparza to accept alternative IDs such as Faith IDs, passports, and matricula consular.

agenda_items.title: Indigenous Peoples Day Proclamation, Neighbor Spotlight, Storm Recovery, and Dillard Teer Tribute
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented recognitions for planning volunteers, the Green Machine, Indigenous Peoples Day (proclaiming Oct. 15, 2018), Neighbor Spotlight recipient Victor Velazquez Luna, and Eddie Davis's Bells Across Durham WWI centennial proposal. Mayor Schewel also thanked Duke Energy crews for restoring 43,500 homes after Tropical Storm Michael and led a moment of silence for late civic leader Dillard Teer.

agenda_items.title: Annual Performance Evaluations and Salary Approvals for Charter Officers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following annual performance evaluations, Mayor Schewel announced and Council unanimously approved 7-0 annual salaries for the City Manager ($243,503), City Attorney ($223,982), and City Clerk ($92,700). Mr. Dixon was also sworn onto the Racial Equity Task Force.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Refuse Vehicles, Dump Trucks with Snow Plows, Tree Removal, ST-270C Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, covering minutes, five automated refuse collection vehicles, dump trucks with snow plows and spreaders, city tree removal services, and contract amendment #3 for ST-270C. Excluding Items 4, 5, and 6 (and Item 14 on the public hearing docket), Council passed the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 619 Herndon Road (City Fire Station)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Carla Rosenberg presented the City's General Services Department request to rezone 2.2 acres at 619 Herndon Road from PDR 3.322 to RS-20 to allow construction of a fire station (requiring a subsequent Board of Adjustment minor special use permit), following a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. With no public speakers, Council passed both the consistency statement and zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — $750,000 Grant to Durham Community Land Trustees (DCLT)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 4, supporting Northeast Central Durham housing rehabilitation but urging the City to tie the $750,000 grant to paid vocational carpentry and construction jobs ($12-$15/hour) for young Black men following two recent fatal shootings in her neighborhood. Mayor Schewel and DeDreana Freeman affirmed her concerns and noted staff would review hiring practices before Council approved the grant 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Park at Southpoint Street Impact Fee Credit Extension Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: George Stanziale pulled Item 5 on behalf of Revial LLC (auto park at NC 751 and I-40), seeking a three-year (or one-year) extension of 2005 street impact fee credits that expired in August 2018 after 13 years including recession tolling. Transportation Director Bill Judge explained that City Code only permits an extension when delayed by a capital improvement thoroughfare project, which did not apply; Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, and DeDreana Freeman concurred against granting an exception (with Freeman cautioning that 'equal is not always fair'), voting 7-0 to approve staff's denial recommendation.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Ordinance Regulating Shared Active Transportation Companies (E-Scooters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bird representative Servando Esparza thanked Council for the shared active transportation permitting ordinance, prompting pointed questioning from Mark-Anthony Middleton, Steve Schewel, Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Charlie Reece regarding Bird's 18+ age policy (vs. Durham's 16+ ordinance) and its refusal to scan Faith IDs, passports, or matricula consular. While Council agreed not to halt the permitting ordinance so staff could begin implementation, Charlie Reece moved approval 7-0 while emphasizing that accepting inclusive IDs remains a Council priority.

votes.item_title: Annual Salaries for City Manager ($243,503), City Attorney ($223,982), and City Clerk ($92,700)
votes.discussion_detail: Following annual evaluations, Council unanimously approved the upcoming year's salaries for all three charter officers.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 10-13, excluding pulled Items 4, 5, and 6)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 4, 5, and 6.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Consistency Statement for 619 Herndon Road Zoning Map Change (Fire Station)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for rezoning 619 Herndon Road.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Ordinance Amending the UDO for 619 Herndon Road (PDR 3.322 to RS-20)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously rezoned 2.2 acres at 619 Herndon Road to RS-20 to permit a future fire station.

votes.item_title: Item 4: Grant to Durham Community Land Trustees ($750,000) for Housing Rehabilitation
votes.discussion_detail: Following Victoria Peterson's plea for local vocational construction jobs for young Black men, Council unanimously approved the $750,000 grant to DCLT.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Approve Staff Recommendation Denying Park at Southpoint Street Impact Fee Credit Extension
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 7-0 to adopt staff's recommendation denying Revial LLC's request to extend expired 2005 street impact fee credits.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Ordinance Establishing Permitting Procedure for Shared Active Transportation Companies
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Charlie Reece after extensive council questioning of Bird on Faith IDs, passports, and matricula consular acceptance, the ordinance passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 1, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: On October 1, 2018, the Durham City Council issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Energy Efficiency Day, and National Arts and Humanities Month, received a report on Durham's Hurricane Florence deployment in Wilmington, and administered an oath of office before passing the consent agenda 7-0 (with Items 3, 9, 11, 13, and 14 pulled). Council unanimously approved 7-0 Racial Equity Task Force appointments (Item 3) after public speakers Trevor Wells and Donald Ray Nolan Jr. demanded accountability in the shooting death of NCCU senior DeAndre Ballard and alleged police profiling, prompting DeDreana Freeman to call for roundtables with armed apartment security guards and Mark-Anthony Middleton to affirm active vigilance. Council also passed all four remaining pulled procurement and easement items (Items 9, 11, 13, and 14) 7-0 following DeDreana Freeman's inquiries into vendor and contractor workforce diversity.

agenda_items.title: Hispanic Heritage Month, Energy Efficiency Day, Arts & Humanities Month, Hurricane Florence Report, and Oath of Office
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel read proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month (Sept. 15-Oct. 15), Energy Efficiency Day (Oct. 5), and National Arts and Humanities Month, and Council heard remarks on Hurricane Florence relief patrols and supply distribution in Wilmington. An oath of office was administered to Ms. Vaidara at 00:39:58.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Audits, Budget Carryover, Police Vehicles, Hope Valley Roundabout & NC 751 Utility Agreement)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda including minutes, Housing Appeals Board and Sesquicentennial Honors Commission appointments, June 2018 departmental/facilities/Housing for New Hope audits, FY17-18 budget carryover ordinances, the August 2018 bid report, a 64-police-vehicle contract with Haresty-Hilderton LLC, and utility agreements for Hope Valley Road and NC 751/University Drive. Council approved the consent slate (excluding pulled Items 3, 9, 11, 13, and 14) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Racial Equity Task Force Appointments and Police/Security Accountability Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Trevor Wells and Donald Ray Nolan Jr. praised the Racial Equity Task Force while demanding Civilian Police Review Board reform (citing HB 193) and answers regarding the fatal shooting of NCCU senior DeAndre Ballard by Campus Crossing security and alleged police tailing. City Manager Tom Bonfield confirmed an active police investigation awaiting lab reports, DeDreana Freeman urged roundtables with armed security companies, and Mark-Anthony Middleton affirmed Council vigilance before Council approved the appointments 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Contract with Freese and Nichols, Inc. for South Durham Phase 3 Hydraulic Model
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman questioned the absence of MWBE/WBE goals on the engineering contract and asked that workforce statistics for both Freese and Nichols and subconsultant Stewart be included in future reports. Staff agreed to include subconsultant statistics going forward, and Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Purchase and Maintenance Agreement with Sharp Business Systems of NC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman commended Sharp Business Systems of North Carolina for strong gender and racial diversity across staffing levels. Council then unanimously approved the multifunctional devices purchase and maintenance agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Contract with Transource Inc. for 11 Replacement Dump Trucks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman questioned Fleet Management Director Joe Clark about missing workforce statistics and low vendor diversity with Transource Inc. Mr. Clark noted marked diversity improvement over two years and ongoing vendor conversations, after which Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Temporary Construction Easement and Fence Donation with Miracle League of the Triangle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman asked General Services Director Stephen Hicks about collecting workforce statistics from Capitol Broadcasting / American Tobacco for the Durham Miracle Athletic Park easement. Mayor Schewel suggested raising routine contractor workforce inquiries during work sessions when vendors and staff are present (with Freeman noting she had missed the prior work session), and Council approved the item 7-0 after repeating an electronic vote.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-2, 4-8, 10, 12, 15, excluding pulled Items 3, 9, 11, 13, and 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding Items 3, 9, 11, 13, and 14.

votes.item_title: Item 3: Racial Equity Task Force Appointments
votes.discussion_detail: Following public testimony on police and private security accountability in the DeAndre Ballard case, Council unanimously approved the Racial Equity Task Force appointments 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Contract with Freese and Nichols, Inc. for South Durham Phase 3 Hydraulic Model
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the Freese and Nichols engineering contract after requesting subconsultant workforce statistics in future reports.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Purchase and Maintenance Agreement with Sharp Business Systems of North Carolina
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the Sharp Business Systems multifunctional devices contract after praising its workforce diversity.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Contract with Transource Inc. for 11 Replacement Dump Trucks
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the dump truck contract with Transource Inc. following Fleet Management's discussion of vendor diversity efforts.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Temporary Construction/Grading Easement and Fence Donation with Miracle League of the Triangle
votes.notes: Re-voted due to electronic voting system issue.
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the Miracle League easement and fence donation 7-0 on a re-vote after discussing work-session review of contractor workforce statistics.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 17, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting on September 17, 2018 in the wake of Hurricane Florence, the Durham City Council recognized PAC-3 neighborhood safety volunteers and commended city employees, the Hillside High School shelter, and the Emergency Operations Center for storm preparedness before approving the consent agenda 7-0. On Item 9, after hearing Bike Durham advocate James Nishimoto and Bird representative Servando Esparza regarding electric scooter regulations, Council voted 7-0 to refer the shared active transportation permitting ordinance to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) for input. Council unanimously passed all three motions (7-0 each) for consolidated annexation Item 17, the Southeast Regional Lift Station annexation (Item 18), and the AAA Storage annexation near Junction Road (Item 20), referred a withdrawn Christian Avenue street closing (Item 19) back to administration without a vote, and voted 7-0 to close a 330.08-foot portion of K Street needed for the Durham-Orange Light Rail right-of-way (Item 21).

agenda_items.title: PAC-3 Safety Recognition and Hurricane Florence Emergency Response Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized neighborhood safety volunteers coordinating with DPD and PAC-3 and noted Constitution Week. City Manager Tom Bonfield, Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Members Alston and Reece praised city staff, the Emergency Operations Center, and volunteers at the Hillside High School emergency shelter for their Hurricane Florence response.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Appointments, DCLT & Habitat Housing Contracts, Triangle Water Supply Partnership, Sibiu Sister City)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read consent items including minutes, Durham Housing Authority, Human Relations Commission, and Recreation Advisory Commission appointments, DCLT (1700 Merrymac St) and Habitat for Humanity housing contracts, the Triangle Water Supply Partnership MOA, Carolina Assisted Living utility extension, and the Sibiu, Romania sister city proposal. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Regulating Shared Active Transportation Companies (E-Scooters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bike Durham board member James Nishimoto supported the scooter permitting ordinance and called for protected bike lanes, while Bird senior manager Servando Esparza supported the ordinance while asking Council to revisit the $100-per-scooter fee and noting Bird's low-income One Bird program. Council Member Charlie Reece, joined by Vernetta Alston, requested deferring action so Durham's Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) could review the draft, and Council voted 7-0 to refer the ordinance back for BPAC input.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Zoning Map Change (Public Hearing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on consolidated annexation Item 17 with no registered speakers or public opposition. Council unanimously voted 7-0 on the annexation ordinance, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Southeast Regional Lift Station
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith presented the consolidated annexation and rezoning for the Southeast Regional Lift Station. With no public speakers or council objections, Council approved the annexation ordinance, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Christian Avenue Street Closing (Withdrawn)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young reported that the applicant withdrew the Christian Avenue street closing request late the prior week. With City Attorney concurrence, Mayor Schewel referred Item 19 back to the administration without a formal vote.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — AAA Storage (Junction Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented AAA Storage's voluntary annexation and rezoning to Industrial Light with a two-story height limit, noting the Planning Commission voted 11-0 and the project would be immediately revenue-positive. Responding to DeDreana Freeman's flooding question on Junction Road, landscape architect Pam Porter confirmed there is no floodplain on site, and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — K Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg recommended permanently closing a 330.08-linear-foot portion of K Street to combine with adjacent properties, confirming for Council that the right-of-way lies within the planned Durham-Orange Light Rail corridor. With no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the closure order 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Refer Shared Active Transportation Permitting Ordinance to BPAC
votes.discussion_detail: Following Charlie Reece's request supported by Vernetta Alston, Council unanimously referred the shared active transportation (e-scooter) ordinance to BPAC for feedback.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Annexation Ordinance (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the annexation ordinance for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Consistency Statement (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Ordinance Amending the UDO (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the UDO zoning amendment for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Ordinance Annexing Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved annexing the Southeast Regional Lift Station into the City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Consistency Statement for Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Southeast Regional Lift Station.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO zoning amendment for the Southeast Regional Lift Station.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Annexing AAA Storage and Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the voluntary annexation and utility extension agreement for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Consistency Statement for AAA Storage
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Amending the UDO for AAA Storage (Industrial Light)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved Industrial Light zoning with a two-story limit for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Order Permanently Closing a 330.08-Linear-Foot Portion of K Street
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously ordered the permanent closure of the 330.08-foot K Street segment within the planned light rail corridor.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 4, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 4, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council honored late civic and educational leader Dr. Phail Wynn Jr. (highlighting his work on the housing trust fund and early childhood education), proclaimed September 2018 as National Recovery Month, and announced five vacancies on the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission. Council unanimously passed the consent agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 3 and 8) and passed 7-0 both motions for UDO text amendment TC18-00003 adopting revised FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels to maintain National Flood Insurance Program eligibility. On pulled Item 3, Mark-Anthony Middleton recommended postponing the Racial Equity Task Force appointments because the proposed slate included only one African American male out of nine applicants; Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman agreed, and Mayor Steve Schewel referred the item by consensus to the September 20 work session while announcing plans to nominate Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair. On pulled Item 8, Council approved 7-0 a $2.9 million Central Park waterline replacement change order (capping total contract cost at $32,008,878.42) after DeDreana Freeman questioned downtown infrastructure prioritization and pressed staff on zero-diversity contractor workforce statistics under the Equal Business Opportunity Program.

agenda_items.title: Tribute to Dr. Phail Wynn Jr., National Recovery Month Proclamation, and Sesquicentennial Honors Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel and speakers paid tribute to late Dr. Phail Wynn Jr. for his housing trust fund advocacy and early childhood education leadership. Mayor Schewel proclaimed September 2018 as National Recovery Month addressing opioid and mental health stigma, and the City Clerk announced five vacancies on the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Board Appointments, GARE Grant, GoDurham Gillig Buses, Rock Quarry & Morreene Parks, Unpaved Road Study)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda including minutes, BPAC, Environmental Affairs Board, and Board of Adjustment appointments, a Government Alliance on Race and Equity (GARE) grant, Gillig replacement buses for GoDurham, financial advisor selection, Rock Quarry Park and Morreene Road Park contracts, BizLibrary e-learning, the unpaved road study (SD-292-2018), and South Ellerbe stormwater demolition. Pulling Items 3 and 8, Council approved the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — UDO Text Amendment: FEMA FIRM Flood Map Updates (TC18-00003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC18-00003 updating Section 8.4 of the UDO to adopt revised FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels effective October 19, 2018, a federal and state requirement to maintain Durham's participation in the National Flood Insurance Program. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 12-0, and Council passed both the consistency statement and UDO amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Racial Equity Task Force Appointments (Deferred to Sept 20 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (who had missed the work session selection) urged Council not to vote because the slate included only one African American male despite nine applying, calling it a systemic teachable moment for Durham's Racial Equity Task Force. Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman supported postponement; Mayor Schewel referred the appointments by unanimous consensus to the September 20 work session, tasked Middleton with leading member discussions, and announced his intent to nominate Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair once membership is settled.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Central Park Waterline Replacement Contract Change Order No. 3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley explained the $2.9 million change order for failing cast-iron lines in the Central Park project (bringing total contract cost up to $32,008,878.42) and outlined upcoming $20 million waterline replacements in East Durham. DeDreana Freeman questioned whether downtown gentrification was driving utility prioritization and pressed Purchasing Manager Ms. Page on why many city supply/vendor contracts report zero people of color despite the Equal Business Opportunity Program ordinance; Mayor Schewel echoed concern over industry capacity gaps before Council approved the change order 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-2, 4-7, 10-16, excluding pulled Items 3 and 8)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 3 and 8.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment TC18-00003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for adopting revised FEMA flood insurance maps.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Adopting UDO Text Amendment TC18-00003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO flood map updates required to maintain NFIP eligibility.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Central Park Waterline Replacement Change Order No. 3 and Additional Contingency (Not to Exceed $32,008,878.42)
votes.discussion_detail: After discussing downtown versus East Durham waterline replacement priorities and EBOP vendor diversity tracking, Council unanimously approved Change Order No. 3.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 20, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 20, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council recognized Freetown/Creole heritage, Neighbor Spotlight awardee Gina Chung, female judicial trailblazers for National Women's Equality Day, and members of the Durham Youth Commission, and unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0 (including acquiring the Durham Beltline corridor, while pulling Item 18). Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2018 Second Quarter Crime Report showing a 13.5% overall drop in Part 1 index crime and a 28% drop in Q2 violent crime despite an increase in homicides. Council unanimously approved 7-0 three planning applications—1900 Ellendale Road II for 15 townhomes (re-voting the UDO ordinance after staff caught a misread motion), 5246 North Roxboro Street for up to 20,000 square feet of commercial space, and the Hillsborough/Cole Mill Road consolidated development with a 90-foot hotel and expanded gas station/car wash—and approved 7-0 the Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau contract for the 2019 Bull City 150 anniversary celebration after incorporating inclusive language requested by DeDreana Freeman.

agenda_items.title: Freetown Heritage, Neighbor Spotlight, Women's Equality Day Judicial Trailblazers, and Durham Youth Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized Freetown/Creole heritage, honored Gina Chung with the Neighbor Spotlight Award, spotlighted two Durham female judicial trailblazers for National Women's Equality Day, and welcomed incoming and returning high school members of the Durham Youth Commission. Shailia Arias was sworn in at 00:36:17.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Boards, RDU FAA Grant, Durham Beltline Acquisition, Building Inspections Online Payment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, including minutes, Carolina Theatre and Recreation Advisory appointments, an RDU Airport Authority FAA AIP grant, proposed acquisition of the Durham Beltline corridor (Item 8), and Building Inspections online payment software. DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 18 (DCVB Bull City 150 contract), and Council passed the remaining consent items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2018 Second Quarter Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported that Part 1 index crime fell 13.5% in the first half of 2018 compared to 2017, with violent crime down 28% in Q2 and double-digit decreases in rapes, robberies, aggravated assaults, larcenies, and auto thefts, though homicides increased. Resident Chris Tiffany also offered public comment before Council thanked the department.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 1900 Ellendale Road II
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Pamela Porter's request on behalf of developer Jim Anthony to rezone 1.3 acres at 1900 Ellendale Road from RS-8 to RU-M(D) for up to 15 townhomes ($200,000-$250,000), following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Javiera Caballero and Mayor Schewel questioned why an off-site BPAC sidewalk suggestion to Dartmouth was declined (Mr. Anthony cited neighboring property owners), and Council passed the consistency statement and corrected RU-M(D) ordinance 7-0 after Wiggins flagged that Mayor Schewel initially read the Item 14 CN-D motion by mistake.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (2 operative motions; UDO re-voted after misread)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5246 North Roxboro Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a request (engineer Jim Clark speaking for the owner) to replace a 1987 family care home restriction on 1.9 acres at 5246 North Roxboro Street with a new CN(D) development plan allowing up to 20,000 square feet of non-TIA commercial space and a transit stop. Planning Commission recommended approval 11-0, and Council passed both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Items — 3578 Hillsborough Road & Cole Mill Road (Holmes Oil / Hotel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Dan Jewell's (Holmes Oil) request covering 5.074 acres at Hillsborough and Cole Mill Roads to rezone 1.563 acres to CG(D) to expand an existing convenience store/gas station with a car wash and 4.141 acres to IL(D) for a 90-foot hotel creating 75-80 jobs, alongside a Future Land Use Map amendment and Christian Avenue connection. Charlie Reece questioned BPAC pedestrian access comments (Jewell cited DOT and utility-pole constraints), and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Contract for Bull City 150 Celebration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by DeDreana Freeman after an afternoon City Attorney memo update, Freeman thanked staff for adding language recognizing First Nations and people of color and questioned DCVB CEO Shelley Green on living wages for hourly event workers and marketing coordination with Parks and Recreation. Mayor Schewel praised the grassroots '150 organizations' approach kicking off at the holiday parade, and Council approved the contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-2, 4-5, 8, 10, excluding pulled Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda including the Durham Beltline corridor acquisition (Item 8) while pulling Item 18 for discussion.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Consistency Statement for 1900 Ellendale Road II
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for 1900 Ellendale Road II.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Ordinance Amending the UDO for 1900 Ellendale Road II (RS-8 to RU-M(D))
votes.notes: Supersedes misread CN-D motion voted at 01:50:16.
votes.discussion_detail: After Mayor Schewel initially read the CN-D motion from Item 14 at 01:49:52 (approved 7-0 at 01:50:16), planner Jake Wiggins flagged the mix-up at 01:50:51 and Council re-voted 7-0 to adopt the correct RU-M(D) ordinance for 1900 Ellendale Road II.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Consistency Statement for 5246 North Roxboro Street
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for 5246 North Roxboro Street.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Ordinance Amending the UDO for 5246 North Roxboro Street (CN-D)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the updated CN-D development plan permitting up to 20,000 sq ft of commercial floor area.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Resolution Amending Future Land Use Map for Hillsborough & Cole Mill Road
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously amended the Future Land Use Map from Commercial to Industrial for the hotel tract.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Consistency Statement for Hillsborough & Cole Mill Road
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Hillsborough & Cole Mill Road rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Hillsborough & Cole Mill Road (CG-D and IL-D)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the zoning ordinance for the convenience store/car wash and 90-foot hotel project.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Contract with Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau for 150th Anniversary Celebration (2019)
votes.discussion_detail: Following City Attorney edits adding First Nations and people-of-color inclusivity language and review of living wage compliance, Council unanimously approved the DCVB contract.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 6, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly five-hour meeting on August 6, 2018, the Durham City Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 (including the CEDAW resolution) and unanimously approved the 15-member Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee and an Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment 7-0. In a major 2-5 split vote on Item 23, Council rejected $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds for Excelsior Classical Academy—with Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Vernetta Alston voting Nay—over charter school funding impacts on Durham Public Schools and TeamCFA governance ties. Council approved 5123 Chin Page Road (Item 24), Garrett Road consolidated annexation (Item 33), and pulled bike/Beltline agreements (Items 10 and 12) 7-0, while passing the Boone Street closing (Item 25), K Street closing (Item 26), and both motions for the Rolling Dale rezoning (Item 27, despite troubling conflict-of-interest concerns) 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman dissenting on each. Finally, Council adopted the Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan (Item 28) while directing staff to return in 90 days with an engagement roadmap for a racial equity plan by a 6-1 vote, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Javiera Caballero voting Nay in favor of an immediate pause.

agenda_items.title: Breastfeeding & CEDAW Resolutions, City Ranking, Consent Agenda, and Committee Appointments (Items 2 & 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented a Breastfeeding Coalition proclamation, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read the CEDAW resolution supporting women's human rights, and Council celebrated Durham ranking seventh among 150 cities nationally. Council approved the consent agenda 7-0 (pulling Items 10 and 12), approved the 15-member Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee slate 7-0 (after holding slots for DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton), and approved an Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — $20M Education Revenue Bonds for Excelsior Classical Academy (Public Finance Authority)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd and bond counsel Mary Nash Rusher presented a TEFRA hearing for up to $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds via Wisconsin's Public Finance Authority (chosen for a 40-year maturity) with no city financial liability. Five council members (Charlie Reece, Vernetta Alston, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, and Steve Schewel) opposed lending the City's tax-exempt financing stamp to a charter school affiliated with TeamCFA and diverting students/funding from Durham Public Schools, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman argued denying tax-exempt refinancing harmed current Durham students; the resolution failed 2-5.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed 2-5 (Middleton & Freeman Aye; Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Caballero, Alston Nay)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5123 Chin Page Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented Charlie Yokley's request to rezone one acre at 5123 Chin Page Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) without a development plan to match adjacent properties, following an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation. DeDreana Freeman questioned tree preservation and the trend of speculative rezonings without development plans before Council passed both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Boone Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Mark and Madison Marvelli's request to permanently close 296 linear feet of unbuilt Boone Street right-of-way between Latta/Lassiter and Dixon Streets containing an existing concrete driveway encroachment. Jillian Johnson and DeDreana Freeman questioned how unpermitted surface and underground encroachments occur in public rights-of-way, and Council passed the closure order 6-1 with Freeman voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — K Street Closing (Duke University Adjacent)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented Ronald Carpenter's request to close 766.81 linear feet of K Street surrounded by Duke University parcels while retaining a sanitary sewer easement. DeDreana Freeman questioned sewer line access enforcement, and Mayor Schewel criticized Duke for leaving the adjacent former city soccer field vacant for a decade while still backing the closure; moved by Mark-Anthony Middleton, the order passed 6-1 with Freeman voting Nay (announced by the clerk as '6-0 with Council Member Freeman voting no').

agenda_items.title: Resumed Public Hearing — Rolling Dale Zoning Map Change (602 & 606 West NC 54)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming a continued public hearing on a 6.65-acre rezoning from RS-20 to PDR 3.94 for 25 townhomes with added 40-foot tree conservation, 70-foot southern setback, and double silt fencing, Council heard the City Attorney report that Durham County's Attorney found no county ethics violation when a Planning Commissioner who voted on the case later represented the applicant. While Mayor Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Vernetta Alston expressed concern that the process appeared tainted, six members judged the proffered buffers superior to by-right development; DeDreana Freeman dissented on both votes (6-1), arguing PDR rezoning is discretionary and threatens waterways.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dale McKeel and Transportation Director Terry Bellamy presented the TIGER-funded Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan after extensive public comment on displacement and equity. Council debated community calls to pause adoption until an equity plan was completed: six members supported adopting the conceptual plan while directing staff to return in 90 days with a community engagement roadmap for a racial equity plan (with Mark-Anthony Middleton clarifying an engagement plan vs. year-long task force work and DeDreana Freeman emphasizing jobs planning), whereas Javiera Caballero voted Nay to honor DOST advocates' call for a pause.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Garrett Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented the Garrett Road consolidated annexation and rezoning (including a $2,500 proffer to Durham Public Schools and an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation). Council discussed traffic signal and sidewalk needs along Garrett Road before approving all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items — Neighborhood Bicycle Routes Design (C-5605I) and Durham Beltline Supplemental Agreement (EB-5504)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved Item 10 (neighborhood bicycle routes design contract, pulled by Adela Ortiz) 7-0. On Item 12 (Durham Beltline supplemental municipal agreement), speakers including Ms. Ortiz urged ensuring 'super-excluded' residents are included and protected from displacement before Council approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 6-9, 11, 14-21, excluding pulled Items 10 and 12)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda including the CEDAW resolution and DHA pre-development grant, excluding pulled Items 10 and 12.

votes.item_title: Item 2: Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee Appointments (15 Members)
votes.discussion_detail: After holding votes open for Freeman and Middleton to participate, Council unanimously approved the 15-member slate (five from each ward).

votes.item_title: Item 5: Audit Services Oversight Committee Appointment

disagreements.issue: Tax-Exempt Conduit Bond Approval for Excelsior Classical Academy Charter School (Item 23)
disagreements.summary: Council split 2-5 on approving a TEFRA resolution enabling Excelsior Classical Academy to issue up to $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds via Wisconsin's Public Finance Authority.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the conduit bond resolution because the City bears no financial liability and denying tax-exempt refinancing penalizes Durham students already attending the school.
side_a_arguments: The school already holds a state charter and owns the building on an interim loan; denying tax-exempt bonds will not prevent expansion and only forces taxable debt that pulls operating funds away from students.
Municipal TEFRA hearings should not be used as a philosophical foil against charter schools when the City contributes zero public dollars and has no jurisdiction over education policy.
Withholding financing leaves the school more financially vulnerable to outside management lender TeamCFA.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the conduit bond resolution because the City should exercise its discretion not to lend a municipal financing tool to charter school expansion.
side_b_arguments: Charter school expansion diverts per-pupil tax dollars and families away from Durham Public Schools, which serve the majority of low-income and Black and brown students.
Excelsior has ongoing financial ties (forgivable loans and a voting board seat) to TeamCFA, whose state takeover politics threaten local public schools.
The school has alternative taxable or governmental financing options without Durham City Council's official stamp of approval.
disagreements.resolution: Motion failed 2-5 at 01:16:26.

disagreements.issue: Boone Street and K Street Right-of-Way Closings and Encroachment Enforcement (Items 25 & 26)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 on both street closing orders (Boone Street and K Street), with DeDreana Freeman dissenting over right-of-way encroachment enforcement and utility/drainage oversight.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the permanent street closures because both met UDO standards, raised no agency objections, and retained required sewer easements.
side_a_arguments: Boone Street was an unbuilt paper street where closing legally remedies an existing driveway encroachment.
On K Street, the City retains a full sanitary sewer easement ensuring maintenance access even though Duke University's adjacent field has sat vacant.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose closing the public rights-of-way due to weak proactive enforcement against surface and underground encroachments.
side_b_arguments: Allowing unpermitted driveways and drainage/underground encroachments to be cured only retroactively via street closures reflects inadequate right-of-way patrol and enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: Both Boone Street and K Street closure orders passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: Rolling Dale Zoning Map Change (RS-20 to PDR 3.94) and Process Ethics Concerns (Item 27)
disagreements.summary: Following a County Attorney review finding no formal ethics violation when a Planning Commissioner who voted on Rolling Dale later represented the developer, Council split 6-1 in approving the rezoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve PDR 3.94 rezoning on its merits despite process concerns because proffered tree buffers, setbacks, and double silt fencing protect neighbors better than by-right single-family development.
side_a_arguments: The County Attorney confirmed no county ethics violation occurred and Council could decide impartially on the merits.
Proffered 40-foot southern tree conservation, 70-foot setbacks, 34% impervious cap, and double silt fencing offer stronger protections than by-right RS-20 single-family construction.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning to PDR 3.94 and keep existing RS-20 zoning to protect waterways and neighborhood stability.
side_b_arguments: Moving from RS-20 to PDR 3.94 is a discretionary legislative action, not a by-right entitlement.
Higher density and grading pose avoidable stormwater and waterway risks to the surrounding community.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and zoning ordinance passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan — Immediate Adoption with 90-Day Engagement Directive vs. Pause for Equity Planning (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to adopt the conceptual Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan while directing staff to return in 90 days with an engagement process for a racial equity plan, with Javiera Caballero voting Nay in favor of pausing adoption.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the conceptual master plan now while directing staff to return within 90 days with a community engagement roadmap to build a racial equity plan before design/construction.
side_a_arguments: Construction is 1.5 to 2 years away, leaving ample time to co-create an equity plan covering affordable housing, local hiring, and corridor engagement before asphalt is laid.

Gentrification is already accelerating citywide regardless of the trail; adopting the master plan preserves federal TIGER/transportation momentum while committing Council to anti-displacement measures.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pause approval of the master plan in deference to community and DOST advocates calling for equity planning first.
side_b_arguments: As a former Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) commissioner and trail advocate, felt compelled to honor residents and DOST members requesting an explicit pause before adoption.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 at 04:31:15.
