meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 16, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 16, 2018 regular meeting, the Durham City Council seated newly appointed At-Large Council Member Javiera Caballero and honored retiring City Clerk D. Ann Gray with a proclamation and tributes recognizing her service and staff stability. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0), funding affordable housing awards for CASA and Durham Community Land Trustees, downtown wayfinding, employee benefits, a HIDTA grant amendment, sidewalk and street resurfacing contracts, and Esri software maintenance. Following an extensive public hearing on Item 12 (2101 House Avenue), Council voted unanimously 7-0 across three separate motions to amend the Future Land Use Map, adopt a consistency statement, and approve rezoning for a 78-unit multifamily project after the developer proffered reserving 50% of units for 10 years at 80% and 100% AMI for City, County, and Durham Public Schools employees. The meeting concluded with a non-agenda appeal from resident Barbara Lofton requesting assistance distributing space heaters to low-income seniors.

agenda_items.title: Seating and Remarks of Newly Appointed Council Member Javiera Caballero
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel invited newly appointed At-Large Council Member Javiera Caballero to take her seat on the dais and offer remarks. Council members noted that her formal appointment motion had been completed at the preceding special meeting and welcomed her to the council.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation and Retirement Tribute for City Clerk D. Ann Gray
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read a proclamation honoring retiring City Clerk D. Ann Gray for her long service to Durham. Council members praised her institutional knowledge, guidance at work sessions, and leadership of an office with virtually no staff turnover and strong customer service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Affordable Housing Funds, Wayfinding, Employee Benefits, HIDTA Grant, Sidewalks & Streets, Esri)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, covering the 2017 municipal primary election, HOME CHDO funds for CASA (formerly Community Alternatives for Supportive Housing), dedicated housing and HOME CHDO funds for Durham Community Land Trustees projects on Kent Street, a downtown Durham Wayfinding Program grant agreement, 2018-2021 employee benefits recommendations, a 2016 HIDTA grant project ordinance amendment, 2018 sidewalk repairs (Contract SW-62) and street repaving (Contract ST-285), and an Esri software maintenance agreement. No items were pulled, and the consent slate was approved by electronic vote with newly seated Council Member Caballero participating.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item for 2101 House Avenue (FLUM Amendment, Consistency Statement, and Zoning Map Change)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Jamie Sanyak) presented a Future Land Use Map amendment and rezoning for a 5.65-acre parcel at 2101 House Avenue to Residential Urban Multifamily with a development plan capping density at 78 units, resolving encroaching parking easements, and extending the Merrimack Street water line. Developer representative Dan Jule (for Broadmont Group) proffered reserving 25% of units at 80% AMI and 25% at 100% AMI for 10 years, with a 90-day pre-lease marketing period for City, County, and Durham Public Schools staff, drawing support from Phil Saab and Lizzie Ellis-Furlong (Durham Literacy Center). Opponent Lanier Blum questioned whether 80-100% AMI rents truly address low-income housing needs, criticized the lack of direct renter notification, and urged off-site sidewalks and relocating the driveway off Merrimack Street; Planning staff agreed to bring renter notification options to JCCC, and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Non-Agenda Request: Heating Assistance for Durham Seniors (Barbara Lofton)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Barbara Lofton addressed Council regarding seniors lacking adequate winter heat and relying on unsafe heaters, requesting help from the city, churches, and residents to supply space heaters in coordination with the Durham Sheriff's Department. Council members thanked her for her advocacy on behalf of seniors and arranged to follow up after the meeting.

votes.item_title: Item 12 (2101 House Avenue): Future Land Use Map Amendment to Medium High Density Residential
votes.notes: First of three required motions for consolidated Item 12.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing and council discussion on workforce housing definitions, annual compliance monitoring, Merrimack Street traffic, off-site sidewalks, and renter notification procedures, Council closed the public hearing and moved to adopt the resolution amending the Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map from Medium Density Residential (6-12 units/acre) to Medium High Density Residential (8-20 units/acre). The motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12 (2101 House Avenue): Adoption of Consistency Statement
votes.notes: Second of three required motions for consolidated Item 12.
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded to adopt the consistency statement for the 2101 House Avenue rezoning request, passing unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12 (2101 House Avenue): Zoning Map Change to Residential Urban Multifamily with Development Plan and Proffers
votes.notes: Third of three required motions for consolidated Item 12; includes developer proffers (50% workforce units at 80%/100% AMI for 10 years, 90-day pre-lease period for public employees, and covered bike parking/pedestrian access).
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded to adopt the requested zoning map change from Residential Suburban Multifamily, Residential Urban Multifamily, Commercial Center, and Commercial Neighborhood with a development plan to Residential Urban Multifamily with a development plan including the developer's proffered workforce housing and site commitments. Following the 7-0 vote, Mayor Schewel urged the developer to still consider sidewalk improvements along the Shoppers Street frontage.
